### Inquiry
Whenever you wish to 225 make an **inquiry** regarding matters, take a bronze vessel—either a bowl or a vial, whichever you wish—and pour in water. If you are calling upon the heavenly gods, use rain water; if the earthly gods, sea water; if Osiris or Sarapis, river water; if the dead, spring water. Holding 230 the vessel upon your knees, pour in green olive oil <note>original: "omphakinon" — oil made from unripe olives</note>, and leaning over the vessel yourself, speak the following formula and call upon whichever god you wish. Ask about whatever you desire, and he will answer you and tell you about everything. When he has finished speaking, release him 235 with the formula of dismissal. You will marvel at the use of this very procedure. # IV 244—290
## 6
<meta>Greek Magical Papyri</meta>

You well know, O greatest king and leader of magicians, that this is the most excellent name of Typhon <note>Typhon is the Greek identification for the Egyptian god Seth, the god of storms, chaos, and the desert.</note>, before whom the earth, the abyss, the underworld, the heavens, <margin>245</margin> the sun, the moon, the visible choir of stars, and the entire world tremble—the name which, when spoken, forcibly draws gods and demons to it. This name consists of one hundred letters. Consequently, at your call, whoever you summon—whether a god or a deceased soul—will appear and will answer concerning everything you ask. <margin>250</margin> However, once you have fully learned what you desire, release the god using only the powerful hundred-letter name, and say: ‘Depart, Lord! For the great god, [Name], <note>The text uses "N N" as a placeholder where the practitioner would insert their own name or the name of a specific deity.</note> wills and commands this of you.’ Speak the name, and he will depart. This magical recipe, O greatest king, shall pass to you alone, <margin>255</margin> to be guarded by you personally. ## A Marvelous Love-Binding Spell

Take wax <insert>or clay</insert> from a potter’s wheel and mold two figures, a male and a female. Make the male in the likeness of **Ares** <note>The Greek god of war.</note>, <margin>300</margin> fully armed, holding a sword in his left hand and threatening to strike the right side of her neck. Make the female figure with her arms bound behind her back and kneeling. You shall attach the *ousia* <term>ousia: Literally "essence," this refers to physical material from the target person, such as hair, nail clippings, or a piece of clothing, used to establish a magical link between the doll and the person.</term> upon her head or her neck. <margin>305</margin> Write upon the figure of the woman who is to be led: on the head, '*iseē Iaō ithi oune bridō lōthiōn neboutosoualēth*'; on the right ear, '*ouer mēchan*'; on the left ear, '*libaba oimathothō*'; on the eyes, '*amounabreō*'; on the right eye, <margin>310</margin> '*ōromothiō aēth*'; on the other eye, '*choboue*'; on the right collarbone, '*adeta merou*'; on the right arm, '*ene psa enegraph*'; on the other arm, <margin>Bl. 5v</margin> '*melchiou melchiedia*'; on the hands, '*melchamelchou aēl*'; on the chest, <margin>315</margin> the name of the woman to be led and her mother’s name; on the heart, '*balamin Thōouth*'; below the belly, '*aobēs aphbar*'; on the genitals, '*blichianeoi ouōia*'; on the <margin>320</margin> buttocks, '*pissadara*'; on the soles of the feet, on the right, '*elō*'; on the other, '*elōaioe*'. 

Take thirteen bronze needles and pierce one into the brain, saying: 'I pierce your brain, [Name of woman],' and two into the ears, <margin>325</margin> and two into the eyes, and one into the mouth, and two into the midriff, and one into the hands, and two into the genitals, and two into the soles of the feet, saying each time: 'I pierce such-and-such a limb of [Name of woman], so that she may remember no one except me alone, [Name of practitioner].' <margin>330</margin> 

Take a lead tablet and write the same words and recite them. Tie the tablet to the figures with thread from a loom, making 365 knots, while saying, as you know: '**Abrasax** <note>A powerful solar deity whose name's letters add up to 365 in Greek numerology, representing the days of the year.</note>, hold her fast!' Place the figures, <margin>335</margin> at sunset, near the grave of someone who died prematurely or violently, offering beside it the flowers of the season. The words to be written and recited are as follows:

> I deposit this binding spell with you, gods of the underworld: **Yessemigadōn** and **the Maiden Persephone Ereschigal** <note>Ereschigal is the Mesopotamian queen of the dead, here identified with the Greek Persephone.</note> and **Adonis** of the **Barbaritha**, and **Hermes** of the underworld, <margin>340</margin> **Thoth** *phōkentazepseu aerchthathou misonktaï kalbanachambrē* and to powerful **Anubis** *psirinth*, who holds the keys to the things in Hades, and to the gods and demons of the underworld, and to those who died before their time, both men and women, and to youths and virgins, for year after year, month after month, [day after day...]

### A Marvelous Love-Binding Ritual

Take wax <insert>or clay</insert> from a potter’s wheel and knead two figures, a male and a female. Form the man in the likeness of an armed **Ares**: in his left hand let him hold a sword <margin>300</margin> which he brandishes against the right side of her neck <note>original: 'Schlüsselbeingrube' - the supraclavicular fossa</note>, but let the woman be bound by her arms behind her back and fallen to her knees. Fasten the *ousia* <term>ousia: Material 'essence' from the target person, such as hair or threads from clothing, used to create a sympathetic link.</term> to her head or neck. Write upon the figure of the woman you wish to compel—specifically on her head: (magic words), on her right ear: (magic words), <margin>305</margin> on her left: (magic words), on the face: (magic words), on the right eye: (magic words), on the <margin>310</margin> other: (magic words), on the right collarbone: (magic words), on the right arm: (magic words), on the other: (magic words), on the hands: (magic words), on the breast the name of the woman being <margin>315</margin> compelled after the name of her mother, on the heart: ‘(magic words) **Thôoyth**’ <note>A variant of the Egyptian god Thoth, often associated with writing and magic.</note>, under the abdomen: (magic words), on the genitals: (magic words), on the buttocks: (magic words), on the soles, and specifically <margin>320</margin> on the right: (magic words), on the other: (magic words). And take thirteen bronze needles and stick one into the brain and say: 

> ‘I pierce your brain, [Name],’ 

and stick two into the ears and two into the eyes and one into the mouth and two into the internal organs and one into the hands and two into the genitals, <margin>325</margin> and two into the soles, each time saying: 

> ‘I pierce the respective limb of [Name], so that she thinks of no one except me, [Name], alone,’ 

and take a lead plate and write the same incantation upon it and recite it <margin>330</margin> and bind the plate to the figures with a thread from a loom in 365 knots, saying as you do so: ‘**Abrasax**, hold fast’ <note>**Abrasax** is a powerful deity representing the 365 days of the year.</note> and deposit them at sunset at the burial place of one who died prematurely or who died a violent death; place flowers of the season beside them. The incantation, which is written and spoken: <margin>335</margin>

### Ritual Invocation and Adjuration

<margin>345</margin> ...days from days, hours from hours. I adjure all the spirits <note>original: 'daimonas' - here referring to the spirits of the deceased often thought to inhabit cemeteries</note> in this place to stand beside this spirit; and rouse yourself for me, whoever you are, whether male or female, and go to every place, to every street, <margin>350</margin> and to every house, and bring and bind: bring [Name], whom [Name] bore, whose *ousia* <term>ousia: physical 'essence' like hair or clothing used to link the magic to the target</term> you hold, loving me, [Name], whom [Name] bore. Let her not be sexually active with another, nor let her find pleasure with another man, except with me alone, [Name], <margin>355</margin> so that [Name] might not be able to drink or eat, nor to show affection, nor to endure, nor to find peace, nor to find sleep, [Name], without me, [Name]. For I adjure you by the name that is fearful and trembling, the name which the earth, upon hearing, shall open, the name which the spirits, <margin>360</margin> upon hearing, shall be terrified by in fear, the name which the rivers and the rocks, upon hearing, shall be shattered by.

I adjure you, spirit of the dead, whether male or female, by **Barbaritha chenmbra barouch-ambra** and by **Abrat Abrasax seseggen barpharangēs** and by the glorious **auia mari** <margin>365</margin> and by **Marmareōth Marmarauōth Marmaraōth marechthana amarza; maribeuth**. Do not ignore my commands and these names, spirit of the dead, but <margin>370</margin> rouse yourself from the rest that holds you, whoever you are, whether male or female, and go to every place, to every street, to every house, and bring [Name] to me. Restrain her from eating and drinking, and <margin>375</margin> do not let [Name] experience any other man for pleasure—not even her own husband—except for me alone, [Name]. Rather, drag [Name] by her hair, by her guts, by her soul to me, [Name], at every hour of time, by night and by day, until <margin>380</margin> she comes to me, [Name], and [Name] remains inseparable from me. Accomplish this; bind her for the entire time of my life and compel [Name] to be my servant, [Name], and let her not stray from me for a single hour of time. <margin>385</margin> If you perform this for me, I will give you rest quickly.

For I am **Barbar Adonai**, he who hides the stars, the bright-shining one who holds the heavens, the lord of the world: **aththoui iathouin selbiuōth; Aōth sarbathiouth iatthierath <margin>390</margin> Adonai ia roura bia bi biotē athōth Sabaōth nauiapha amarachthi; satama; Zauaththeiē serphō ialada ialē ebēsi; iattha; maradtha; achilththee chouō sē ēachō; kansaosa; alkmouri; <margin>395</margin> thur; thaōos; siechē**. I am **Thoth** <note>The Egyptian god of wisdom and magic, identified here with the practitioner</note> **osomai**. Bring, bind [Name]—loving, desiring, longing for [Name] (add the common formulas), because I adjure you, spirit of the dead, by the fearful and great **iaeō baphrenemoun oui larikriphia <margin>400</margin> eueai phirkiralithon uomen er phabōeai**, so that you might bring [Name] to me and join head to head, and join lips to lips, and join belly to belly, and join thigh to thigh...

# IV 455-498 89

...according to your teachings. I call upon your name, Horus <note>The Egyptian solar deity, often identified with Apollo or Helios in this period</note>, who is equal in number <margin>455</margin> to that of the Fates <note>German: *Moiren*. The numerical value (isopsephy) of the following magical name matches the names of the three Fates: Clotho, Lachesis, and Atropos</note> (magical name). Be gracious to me, Forefather, offspring of the world, self-begotten, fire-bringer, gold-glimmering, light-bringer to mortals, ruler <margin>460</margin> of the world, spirit <term>Daimon<note>A divine or supernatural power, not necessarily "evil" in this context</note></term> of the restless fire, imperishable one, golden circle, who sends pure light from his rays upon the earth, send the spirit whom I requested, for [Name] (as you wish).' Another version of the name: (magical name). Another: (magical name). <margin>465</margin>

**To banish anger:**
> 'Will you dare to raise the mighty spear against Zeus?' <note>A line from Homer's Iliad (8.424), used here as a protective or commanding charm</note>

**(Oracle) for friends:**
> 'Let him seize it, so that we do not become a joy to our enemies.' <margin>470</margin> <note>Iliad 10.193</note>
> 'He spoke and guided the stomping horses through the trench.' <note>Iliad 10.564</note>
> 'And the men still twitching in terrible slaughter.' <note>Iliad 10.521</note>
> 'They themselves washed off the abundant sweat in the sea-flood.' <note>Iliad 10.572</note>
> 'Ares endured it, when Otos the violent, along with Ephialtes...' <note>Iliad 5.385</note>

Be gracious to me, Providence <note>Greek: *Pronoia*</note> and Soul <note>Greek: *Psychē*</note>, as I write down these secrets that are not for sale <margin>475</note> but are to be handed down; for my only child, however, I ask for immortality, O initiates <term>Mystai<note>Those who have been initiated into secret religious mysteries</note></term> of this our power (you must, daughter, take juices <margin>480</margin> from plants and spices, which shall [be designated] to you at the end of my holy scripture), which the great god Helios Mithras let me know through his archangel, so that I alone may ascend <margin>485</margin> to heaven at my request and behold everything. The invocation of the prayer is as follows: 'First birth <term>Genesis<note>Greek: *Γένεσις*. Here referring to the origin or the "becoming" of the practitioner's own existence</note></term> of my birth *aeeioyô*, first beginning <term>Archē<note>Greek: *Ἀρχή*. The first principle or source</note></term> of my beginning (cluck three times, whistle three times, [snort?]), spirit <note>Greek: *pneuma*</note> of the spirit, of the spirit within me first (bellow <margin>490</margin> three times), fire, given by God to my mixture of mixtures within me, of the fire within me first (7 vowels), water of the water, of the water within me first (vowels), earth-matter, of the earth-matter within me first (vowels), my, [Name], <margin>495</margin> son of [Name], perfect body, formed by a glorious arm and...

---

<note>Scholarly apparatus notes for lines 475-496: Various scholars debate the reading of "archangel" or "messenger" (αἰητής/αἰτητής). The instructions for vocalizations—clucking (πόππυσον), whistling (σύρισον), and bellowing (μύκησον)—are characteristic of the "Mithras Liturgy" and are intended to mimic divine sounds or command elemental forces. The "7 vowels" refer to the Greek vowels (α ε η ι ο υ ω), which were linked to the seven planets.</note>

<summary>This page contains a charm for subduing anger and a series of Homeric verses used for divination before introducing the "Mithras Liturgy." This liturgy is a ritual of spiritual ascent where the practitioner invokes the elemental components of their own being (spirit, fire, water, earth) to achieve immortality.</summary>

### IV 498--551

...of the incorruptible [spirit] in an unlit and transparent world, both in the inanimate and the animate <note>The Greek *psychōmenōi* refers to things endowed with a *psyche* or soul</note> (magical names: *yēi aui euōie*). 

<margin>500</margin> If it should please you (magical names: *meterta phōth*—or in another version: *methartha phērē*) (magical name: *ierezath*) to transfer me to the immortal generation, following my underlying nature; so that after the <margin>505</margin> present and very urgent need, I may behold the immortal beginning by the immortal spirit (magical name: *anchrephrenne-kouphiri-nch*); by the immortal water (magical names: *erounouï parakounēth*); by the most solid air (magical names: *eioaē psenabōth*); so that I may be reborn in thought <margin>510</margin> (magical names: *kraochrax r oim enarchomai*); and may the holy spirit breathe in me (magical names: *nechthen apotou nechthin arti ēth*); so that I may marvel at the holy fire (magical name: *kyphe* <note>original: *kyphi*. This was a famous incense blend used in Egyptian temples</note>); so that I may gaze upon the abyss of the East, the terrifying water (magical names: *nyō theō echō ouchiechōa*); and may the life-giving and <margin>515</margin> encompassing Aether <note>The "upper air" or "pure air" breathed by the gods</note> (magical name: *arnomēthph*) hear me. 

For I am about to behold today with immortal eyes—I, who was born mortal from a mortal womb, but who has been improved by the mighty power and the <margin>520</margin> incorruptible right hand—by the immortal spirit, the immortal <term>Aeon<note>A personification of eternal time and the totality of the universe</note></term> and Master of the fiery crowns, having been sanctified with holy purifications—I, a holy man—while my human, soul-driven power <margin>525</margin> stands aside for a little while. This power I shall receive back again after the present and urgent bitter necessity which leaves me in no debt <note>Greek: *achreokopēton*. This likely means the practitioner will return to their mortal body "whole" or "without loss"</note>—I, [Name], whose mother is [Name], according to the unchangeable decree of <margin>530</margin> God (magical names: *euē uïa ēēiaō iau iua ieō*). 

Since it is not possible for me, being born mortal, to rise up with the golden brightness of the immortal radiance (magical names: *ōēu aeō ēua eōē uae ōiae*). Stand still, corruptible nature of mortals, and at once <insert>take back</insert> <margin>535</margin> me safe and sound after the inevitable and urgent need. For I am the son (magical names: *psychōn demou prochō prōa*), I am (magical names: *macharph[.]n mou prōpsychōn prōe*).'

Draw breath from the rays, inhaling three times as much as you can, and you will see <margin>540</margin> yourself being lifted up and transcending into the height, so that you seem to be in the middle of the air. You will hear nothing—neither man nor animal <margin>Bl. 8 r. Another</margin> <margin>545</margin> —nor will you see any of the mortals upon the earth in 그 hour, but you will see all things as immortal. For you will see, on that day and at that hour, the divine ordering: the gods who move through the heavens ascending, and others descending. And the path of the visible gods will appear through the disk <note>The sun's disk</note> of my father, the God; likewise, the so-called <margin>550</margin> "pipe," the origin of the ministering wind, will be seen.

### IV 551—607

<margin>551</margin> ...mine; for you will see hanging from the disk what looks like a pipe <note>original: *aulon*. This "pipe" or "tube" is a famous element of the Mithras Liturgy, often interpreted as the source of the wind or a conduit for divine breath.</note>. And toward the regions toward the South-west <note>original: *liba*</note>, it is as if there is an infinite East-wind; but if the wind is allotted to the regions of the East <margin>555</margin>, and the other similarly to those regions, you will see the discharge <note>or "outflow"</note> of the vision. You will see the gods looking intently at you and rushing toward you. But you must immediately place your right finger upon your mouth and say: 'Silence, Silence, <margin>560</margin> Silence, symbol of the living, incorruptible God. Keep me safe, Silence: *NECHTHEIR THANMELOU*.' Then give a long, hissing sound <term>surygmos<note>A ritual whistling or hissing sound intended to evoke a divine presence or represent the sound of the elements.</term>, then make a clicking sound <term>poppysmos<note>A smacking or clicking sound made with the lips, common in ancient magical practices.</term> and say: 'PROPROPHENGĒ MORIOS PRO- <margin>565</margin> PHTHYR PROPHENGĒ NEMETHIRE ARPSENTEN PITĒTMI MEUŌ ENARTH PHURKECHŌ PSYRIDARIŌ TYRĒ PHILBA.' And then you will see the gods looking kindly upon you and no longer rushing at you, but rather proceeding toward their own rank of affairs. When, therefore, you see the upper <margin>570</margin> world <term>kosmos<note>The ordered universe or celestial sphere.</term> clear and vibrating, and no gods or angels rushing forth, expect to hear the crash of a great thunder, so that you are struck with amazement. But <margin>575</margin> say again: 'Silence, Silence (the formula), I am a star wandering with you, and shining out from the depth: *OXY O XERTHEUTH*.' When you have said these things, the disk will immediately expand. After you have said the second formula, where 'Silence, Silence' and the following are said, <margin>580</margin> hiss twice and click twice, and immediately you will see stars coming forward from the disk, five fingers long, very many and filling the whole air. You must say again: 'Silence, Silence.' And when the disk has opened, you will see a fireless <margin>585</margin> circle and fiery doors that are closed. You must immediately recite the following formula while closing your eyes.

**The Third Formula:**
'Hearken to me, hear me, [Name], born of [Name], O Lord, you who have bound together <margin>590</margin> with spirit the fiery bolts of the four-fold girdle <note>original: *tetralizōmatos*. Then whistle in a long <margin>560</margin> whistling sound <term>surygmos<note>A ritual hissing or whistling used to commune with elemental or divine forces.</note></term>, then make a clicking sound <term>poppysmos<note>A smacking or clicking sound made with the lips, often used in ancient magic to attract or appease spirits.</note></term> and say: 'Forward-shining one <note>original: *ZW*</note>, Purple one(?), Forward-shining one <note>original: *ZW*</note>,' and then you will see how the gods look <margin>565</margin> graciously upon you and no longer advance against you, but rather proceed to the proper location of their own activity. ### IV 608—670

...articulated in distinct form by a human tongue, or a mortal sound, or a mortal voice—immortal, living, and honored names: <note>The following are strings of ritual vowels representing the seven planets and cosmic harmony.</note> **eeō oēeō iōō oē ēēō ēēō oē eō iōō oēē eōē ōoē iē ēō oō oē ieō oē ōoē ieō oē ieēō eē iō oē ioē ōēō eoē oeō·ōiē ōiē eō oï iii ēoē ōyē ēōoēe eō ēia aēa eēa ēeeē eeē eeē ieō ēēō oēeeon ēēō ēyō oē eïō ēō ōē ōē ee ooo yiōē.** 

Say all these things with fire and spirit when you are performing the first part; then do the same when beginning the second part, until you complete the seven immortal gods of the world. When you have said these things, you will hear thunder and a shaking of the surrounding air. You will feel yourself being shaken as well. But you must say again: **"Silence!"** <gloss>ritual word</gloss> Then open your eyes and you will see the doors opened and the world of the gods, which is within the doors; as a result of the pleasure and joy of this sight, your spirit will race forward and ascend. 

Standing there, immediately draw in the breath <term>pneuma<note>The 'divine breath' or spirit which the practitioner inhales to achieve a state of inspiration or deification.</note></term> from the divine, gazing into yourself. When your soul is restored, say: **"Come, Lord, Archanchara Phōtaza Pyriphōta Zabythie Etimenmero Phorathēn Eriē Prothri Phorathi."** <note>These are "voces magicae" or magic words, likely derived from corrupted Greek or Egyptian titles meaning things like "Light-bringer" or "Fire-shining."</note> After you have said this, the rays will turn toward you; look into the middle of them. 

When you have done this, you will see a younger god, beautiful in appearance, with fiery hair, wearing a white tunic and a red cloak, and wearing a crown of fire. Immediately greet him with the fiery greeting: 

"Hail, Lord, of great power, of great might, King, greatest of gods, Helios, the Lord of heaven and earth, God of gods! Your breath is strong; your power is strong, Lord. If it pleases you, announce me to the greatest God, the one who begat and created you: that I, **[Name]**, son of **[Mother's Name]**, <note>The text uses "NN" or "So-and-so" as a placeholder for the practitioner's identity.</note> born from a mortal womb and of seminal fluid—and who today has been reborn by you—out of so many thousands having been made immortal in this hour by the will of God, who is exceedingly good, seeks to worship you and prays to you with all human strength." 

<margin>Folio 9 recto</margin> (The prayer continues: "Take along with you the **Horonomos** <term>Horonomos<note>The 'ruler of the hour,' an astrological spirit or deity governing the specific time of the ritual.</note></term> of this day and hour, whose name is **Thrapsiari Morirok**, so that he may appear and give revelation during the favorable hours: **eōrō rōre ōrri ōriōr rōr rōi ōr reōrōri eōr eōr eōr eōre**.") 

When you have said these things, he will come to the celestial pole, and you will see him walking as if on a path. You, however, must gaze and give a long lowing sound, like a horn, exhaling your entire breath and straining your sides. Bellow and kiss the amulets <term>phylaktēria<note>Protective charms or scrolls worn on the body during the ritual.</note></term> and say first to the right: **"Protect me, Prosymiri."** 

After you have said this, you will see doors opening and seven virgins coming from the depths, dressed in fine linen, having the faces of asps. These are called the **Fates of Heaven**, and they hold golden wands. When you see them, greet them in this way: 

"Hail, you seven Fates of Heaven, noble and good virgins, sacred and companions of **Minimirrophor**, most holy guardians of the four pillars. Hail, the first..."

<note>Footnote 609: "immortal living": see Radermacher on Demetrius' *On Style* 72. 610—616: 23 sets of 7 letters; certain patterns repeat, particularly the group "ōoē". 619: Eitrem suggests "beginning." 621: Regarding the "surrounding air," compare PGM VII 508. 622: For the form of the Greek verb "you will feel," see Helbing's grammar. 623: The papyrus refers here to the prayer found at lines 558, 573. 631: These magic words appear to be of Greek construction. 635: Compare Deubner on incubation rituals. 639: The papyrus originally had "melokrator," corrected by Wessely to "megalokratōr" (great ruler).</note>

### IV 608—670

...human tongue, or human sound, or human voice—the eternally living and praiseworthy names: <note>The vowel sequences from the previous page continue here.</note> **'(Vocal series)'**. <margin>610/15</margin> Speak all of this with fire and spirit the first time until the end, and then likewise when you begin for the second time, until you have named all seven immortal gods of the world. <margin>620</margin> When you have spoken this, you will hear thunder and a crashing in the surrounding air; likewise, you will feel yourself being shaken. Then speak again: **'Silence!'** <gloss>ritual formula</gloss>; after this, open <margin>625</margin> your eyes, and you will see the gates open and the world of the gods which is within the gates, so that from the pleasure and joy of the sight, your spirit is carried away and ascends. Now stand still and, looking steadily at the divine being, draw the divine breath <term>pneuma<note>The 'divine breath' or spirit which the practitioner inhales to achieve a state of inspiration or deification.</note></term> into yourself. <margin>630</margin> And once your soul has come to itself again, say: **'Come here, Lord (ZW)!'** <note>ZW stands for *Zauberwort*, a magical name or "word of power."</note> After these words, the rays will turn toward you: look into their center. When you do this, you will see a god, <margin>635</margin> very young, beautiful in form, with hair of fire, in a white garment and a scarlet chlamys <term>chlamys<note>A short mantle or cloak worn by ancient Greeks, often associated with travelers or young men.</note></term>, with a fiery wreath. Immediately greet him with the fire-greeting: <margin>640</margin> **'Hail, Lord, great-mighty, high-powerful King, greatest of the gods, Helios, Lord of heaven and earth, God of gods; mighty is your breath, mighty is your power, Lord. If it please you, announce me to the greatest God, who has begotten and created you: that a human, I, <margin>645</margin> [Name], son of [Mother's Name], born from the mortal womb of [Mother's Name] and from seed-containing life-fluid—and since this (earthly being) is today reborn by you—made immortal among so many thousands in this hour according to <margin>650</margin> the counsel of the exceedingly good God, desires to worship you, and therefore I entreat according to human capacity that you take with you the ruler of this day and hour, whose name is Thrapsiari Morirok, so that he may appear and reveal himself in the good hours (ZW).'** <margin>655</margin> When you have said this, he will go to the pole, and you will see him walking as if on a path. But you, look steadily and let out a long bellowing sound <note>original: "Brüllen"</note>, as if from a horn, giving out all your breath and straining your abdomen, <margin>660</margin> and kiss the amulets and say, first to the right one: **'Protect me (ZW).'** After these words, you will see gates open and see coming from the deep seven virgins in fine linen <term>byssos<note>A very fine, costly fabric made from linen or silk-like fibers, associated with priestly or royal garments.</note></term> garments with snake-faces. They <margin>665</margin> are called 'the Fates of Heaven' and hold golden scepters. If you see this, speak the greeting thus: **'Greetings, you seven Fates of Heaven, noble and kind virgins, holy and living together with the (ZW), <margin>670</margin> you most holy guardians of the four pillars. Hail to you, the first...'**

### IV 671--731

...Chrepsenthaes, hail, the second; Meneseches, hail, the third; Mechran, hail, the fourth; <margin>672^a</margin> Ararmaches, hail, the fifth; Echomme, hail, the sixth; Tichnondaes, hail, the seventh; 'Erou, Rombries.' <note>These are secret names for the seven Fates or celestial weavers mentioned on the previous page.</note> And there also <margin>675</margin> come forward seven other gods having the faces of **black bulls**, wearing linen loincloths and holding seven golden diadems. These are the ones called the **Pole-Lords** <term>polokratores<note>Lords of the celestial pole or axis, responsible for the rotation of the universe.</note></term> of heaven, whom you must likewise greet, each by his own name: 'Hail, <margin>680</margin> you **Guardians of the Pivots**, you holy and mighty youths, who turn the revolving axis of the circle of heaven under a single command, and who send forth thunders and lightnings and bolts of earthquakes and thunderbolts against the tribes of the impious, but to me, who am <margin>685</margin> pious and God-fearing, grant health and wholeness of body, and keenness of hearing and sight, and tranquility in the present good hours of this day, O my lords and great-ruling gods! Hail, the first, Aieronthi; hail, the second, <margin>690</margin> Mercheimeros; hail, the third, Achrichiur; hail, the fourth, Megargilto; hail, the fifth, Chichroalitho; hail, the sixth, Ermichthathops; hail, the seventh, Eorasiche.' And when they take their places on either side <margin>695</margin> in their ranks, gaze into the air and you will see lightnings descending and lights shimmering and the earth shaking, and a **god descending**, immensely great, having a bright appearance, young, golden-haired, in a white tunic and a golden crown <margin>700</margin> and trousers <term>anaxyrides<note>Traditional Persian-style trousers, signaling the god's Eastern/Mithraic identity.</note></term>, holding in his right hand a golden shoulder of a young bull: this is the **Bear** <note>The constellation Ursa Major, which ancient astronomers believed 'turned' the heavens.</note> which moves and turns the heaven, revolving upward and downward according to the hour. Then you will see lightnings flashing from his eyes and stars leaping from his <margin>705</margin> body. And you should immediately give a long **bellowing** <note>A ritual sound, likely imitating a bull, intended to vibrate the body and senses.</note>, straining your belly to move your five senses—a long sound until you are out of breath—bellowing and again kissing <margin>Bl. 9 v.</margin> your protective amulets and saying: 'Mokrimo Pherimophereiri, may my life, [name], remain; <margin>710</margin> dwell in my soul, do not leave me, for Entho Phenen Thropioth commands you.' And gaze at the god while bellowing long, and greet him thus: 'Lord, hail, master of water; hail, founder of <margin>715</margin> the earth; hail, ruler of the spirit; bright-shining, first-shining, Emethiri Artentepi; Theth; Mimeo Uenaro Phurchecho Pseri Dario; Phre Phrelba; give me an oracle, Lord, concerning [mention the matter]. Lord, being **born again**, I pass away; <margin>720</margin> increasing and having increased, I die; born from a life-giving birth, I am dissolved into a state beyond birth and go my way, as you have created, as you have legislated and established as a mystery. I am Pheroura Miouri.' When you have said these things, he will <margin>725</margin> immediately give an oracle. But you will be weak in your soul and will not be yourself when he answers you. He speaks the oracle to you in verse, and after speaking, he will depart; but you stand there speechless, for you will contain all these things in your mind automatically, and then <margin>730</margin> you will remember without fail the things spoken by the great god, even if they were ten thousand!

### IV 731—787

The oracle is given in verses. If you wish to use a **fellow-initiate** <note>Greek: symmystes; a partner in the secret rites</note> so that he alone hears the things spoken along with you, let him remain pure with you for seven days and abstain from meat and the baths. And if you are alone and are undertaking the things spoken by the god, you speak as if in a state of ecstasy, being inspired by the god. 

If you also wish to show him <note>the fellow-initiate</note>, judge whether he is worthy as a man. After using the method, as if being judged on his behalf during the **immortalization** <note>Greek: apathanatismos; the ritual of ascending to the divine state</note>, whisper to him the first speech, of which the beginning is: "First birth of my birth <note>Greek: genesis prōtē tēs emēs geneseōs</note>, AEHIOUŌ." <note>The seven Greek vowels, representing the harmony of the spheres</note>. 

And as an initiate, speak the following things over his head in a toneless voice so that he does not hear, while anointing his face with the **mystery** <note>The "mystery" here refers to the consecrated ointment described later</note>. This immortalization takes place three times a year. But if anyone, O son, should choose to disobey after this instruction, it will no longer be possible for him.

->**Instruction for the Practice:**<-

Taking a **solar scarab beetle** <note>A beetle with twelve rays, symbolizing the hours of the day</note>, the one having the twelve rays, make it be thrown into a deep turquoise-colored vessel <note>Greek: bēsion kallainon; likely a cup made of Egyptian faience or glazed pottery</note> during the "seizing" of the moon <note>likely referring to the moon's waning phase or an eclipse</note>, throwing in with it the seed of the "lotus-womb" <note>Greek: lōtomētras; a specific part of the lotus plant</note> and, having ground it with honey, make a small cake. 

And you will immediately see him <note>the beetle/divine messenger</note> approaching and eating; and when he eats, he immediately dies. Taking this up, cast it into a glass vessel of the finest **rose oil**, as much as you wish. Having spread holy sand in a pure manner, place the vessel upon it and say the name over the vessel for seven days while the sun is at the meridian: 

"I have consecrated you so that your essence <note>Greek: ousia</note> might become useful to me, [Name], alone: IE IA Ē EĒ OU EIA. May you be useful to me alone. For I am PHŌR PHORA PHŌS PHOTIZAAS <note>original: "φωρ φορα φως φοτιζαας" — "phōs" means light, "photiza" suggests illumination</note> (others say: PHŌR PHOR OPHOTHEI ZAAS)."

On the seventh day, taking up the scarab and burying it with myrrh and Mendesian wine and fine linen, deposit it in a bean-field that is full of life. After you have held a feast and joined in the banquet, set aside the ointment in a pure place for the **immortalization**. 

And if you wish to show someone else, have the juice of the plant called **kentritis** <note>A magical herb, often identified as a type of spurge or "centaury"</note>, anointing the face of whomever you wish with it along with rose oil, and he will see so clearly that you will marvel. I have found no greater ritual than this in the world. Ask the god for what you wish, and he will give it to you. 

Now, the "standing-together" <note>Greek: systasis; a formal meeting or introduction to a deity</note> with the great god is as follows: taking the aforementioned *kentritis* herb during the conjunction <note>of the moon</note> occurring in the sign of Leo, take the juice and, having mixed it with honey and myrrh, write the **eight-letter name** <note>An secret name of the god consisting of eight characters</note> upon a leaf of a **Persian tree** <note>The Persea tree, sacred in Egyptian and Hellenistic magic</note>, as it is set down below. 

Having remained pure for three days before, come in the morning toward the sunrise, lick off the leaf while showing it to the sun, and in this way he will listen perfectly. Begin to initiate him <note>the god/the rite</note> during the...

### IV 731—787
7*

Remember the words of the great god, even if the oracle consists of thousands of verses. If you also wish to bring in a fellow-initiate <note>original: "Miteingeweihten"; Greek: symmystēs</note> so that he alone may hear the words with you, let him remain <margin>735</margin> pure with you for seven days and abstain from meat and the bath. But if you are alone and are attempting the spell communicated by the god, speak as if in a state of ecstasy, full of prophetic inspiration. If you also wish to show it to him (the fellow-initiate), judge whether he is beyond doubt <margin>740</margin> worthy as a human being, and apply the same standard as if you yourself were being judged in his place during the **immortalization** <note>original: "Verewigung"; Greek: apathanatismos, the ritual process of becoming divine</note>, and recite to him the prayer that begins thus: 'First origin of my origin, *aeēioyō*' <note>the seven Greek vowels representing the harmony of the spheres</note>. Speak what follows as an initiate over his head in a toneless voice, so that he does not hear it, and anoint <margin>745</margin> his face with the ointment of the mystery. This immortalization may take place three times a year. But should someone, my child, after receiving the instruction, fail to follow it, it will no longer be at his command. <margin>750</margin>

->Instruction on the performance:<- take a **solar scarab beetle** <note>a beetle with twelve rays, symbolizing the hours of the day or signs of the zodiac</note> with the twelve rays, let it fall into a deep vessel made of gold-stone <note>original: "Goldstein"; likely a vessel made of or containing chrysocolla or gold-leaf</note> at the new moon; at the same time, throw in seeds of the lotometra <note>a plant often identified with a type of lotus or clover</note> and honey, grind this up and make <margin>755</margin> a small cake, and immediately you will see it <note>the beetle</note> approach and eat; and when it has eaten, it dies immediately. Then take it out and throw it into a glass vessel with as much of the best rose ointment as you like, spread holy sand in purity and set the vessel upon it, and speak the formula over <margin>760</margin> the vessel for seven days when the sun is at midday: 'I have consecrated you, so that your magical substance may be useful to me, [Name], alone (vowels): to me alone be subservient; for I am (Magical Words) (others: [Magical Words])'. On the seventh <margin>765</margin> day, take the scarab, bury it in myrrh and wine from Mendes <note>an Egyptian city famous for its perfume and wine</note> and in fine linen <note>original: "Byssos"</note>, and keep it in a sprouting bean-bed. But the ointment, after you have provided for (the divinized scarab) and have yourself partaken of the sacrificial meal, preserve in purity for the <margin>770</margin> immortalization ceremony. If you wish to show it to another, take the juice of the plant called 'Kentritis' <note>an unidentified magical herb, possibly a type of verbena or thorny plant</note>, smear the face of the chosen person with it and simultaneously with rose oil, and he will see so clearly that you will be amazed. A stronger magical practice than this I <margin>775</margin> have not found in the world. Ask of the god whatever you want, and he will grant it to you. The union with the great god is as follows: pick the aforementioned Kentritis plant at the new moon when the sun is <margin>780</margin> in Leo, take its juice and mix it with honey and myrrh, and write on a leaf of the Persea <note>a sacred Egyptian tree; original: "περσέα"</note> the eight-lettered name, as it follows; keep yourself pure for three days beforehand and go early toward the East, lick the leaf off, showing it to the <margin>785</margin> sun, and thus he will perfectly hear you. ### IV 788—834

in Leo <note>The zodiac sign</note> during the new moon. The name is this: *i ee oo iai*. Lick 
<margin>790</margin> this, so that you may be protected <note>original: "phylaktēriasthēs"; to be provided with a phylactery or spiritual defense</note>, and having rolled || up the leaf, cast it into the rose oil. Having 
frequently used this procedure, I was utterly amazed. But the god said to me: ‘No longer 
use the ointment, but having thrown it into a river, <term>you must</term> <note>original: "chrē"</note> use it while wearing 
<margin>795</margin> the great mystery || of the beetle which has been revived by the twenty-five <note>Greek: κ̅ϵ̅</note>

The *kentritis* herb <note>An unidentified magical plant, possibly named for its "stinging" or "spur-like" qualities</note> 
<margin>800</margin> grows || from the month of Payni <note>Late May to June in the Egyptian calendar</note> in the regions of 
the Black Land <note>Egypt; "Kemet"</note>; it is similar to the upright vervain. Its identification 
is made as follows: the dark tip of an ibis feather is smeared with the juice, and as 
<margin>805</margin> soon as it is touched, || the feathers fall off. This was found, as the Lord 
revealed, in the Menelaite district at Phalagry <note>A village in the Nile Delta</note> near the embankments 
close to the Besas-herb. It is 
single-stemmed and reddish down to the root, the leaves are rather curly, and 
<margin>810</margin> it has fruit || similar to the cluster of wild asparagus. It is quite similar to the so-called 
*talape*, like wild beet. The protective amulets <note>original: "phylaktēria"</note> are made in 
<margin>815</margin> this manner: write the right one || on the membrane of a black sheep with myrrh-ink, 
and having tied the same with the sinews of the same animal, hang it around yourself; 
but write the left one on the membrane of a white sheep and use it in the same 
<margin>Bl. 10 v.</margin> way. The left one of the 'pleasant-favor' spell is || 
<margin>820</margin> most complete and contains the following citation <note>original: "hypomnēma"; referring here to the list of Homeric verses used as charms</note>: |

->‘So speaking, he drove the single-hoofed horses through the trench;’<- <note>Iliad 10.564</note>
->‘And men gasping in painful slaughter;’<- <note>Iliad 10.521</note>
->‘They themselves washed off their much sweat in the sea;’<- <note>Iliad 10.572</note>

<margin>800</margin>
The plant *Kentritis* <note>A magical herb, likely named for the Greek "kentron" meaning a sting or spur; its identification remains debated among botanists</note> grows from the month of Payni <note>Late May to June</note> in the region of the Black Earth <note>Egypt; "Kemet"</note> and resembles upright pigeon-weed <note>Commonly known as Vervain</note>. It is recognized as follows: if the black tip of an ibis feather is smeared with its juice 
<margin>805</margin>
and soaked, the feathers fall off upon contact. The Lord showed it, and so it was found in the Menelaïte district in Phalagry <note>A village in the Nile Delta</note> at the embankments (of the Nile), near the plant of Besas. It is single-stemmed and reddish-brown down to the root; the leaves are quite woolly, and the 
<margin>810</margin>
fruit is similar to the head of wild asparagus. It is similar to the so-called *Talapês*, like wild mangold. 

The amulets are prepared as follows: write the right one with myrrh ink on the skin of a black sheep, also bind it with tendons of the same animal and hang it around [the neck]; but the left one on the skin of a white sheep and use it in the same way. The left one is completely filled with 'Prosthymêri' <note>A magical name or substance</note> and has the inscription:

<note>Scholarly annotations for lines 1001-1024:</note>
<gloss>1001: The scribe originally wrote 'dagennuthuth' but struck through several letters to correct it to a different vowel sound.</gloss>
<gloss>1004: Scholars suggest 'symbolic form' refers to a specific ritual posture or a pyramid-like arrangement of the letters.</gloss>
<gloss>1006: The instruction to 'speak like a dog-headed ape' likely refers to a rhythmic barking or hooting sound used to greet the sun.</gloss>
<gloss>1010: 'Bêl' is the old Babylonian word for 'Lord.' Other syllables like 'bol' or 'be' may be shortenings of solar names or the word for 'soul' in Coptic.</gloss>
<gloss>1019: 'Balsamês' is a Semitic title for a God of Light (Baal Shamin).</gloss>
<gloss>1022: The magical word 'ninther' likely stems from the Egyptian word for 'the gods.'</gloss>

### IV 1026–1080

...having [the name] Sesengen Barpharangēs <note>A powerful "barbarous" name often associated with solar or underworld deities in these papyri</note>, he who sits within the seven poles <gloss>vowels: a e ē i o u ō</gloss>, he who has a golden crown upon his head, and in his hand a Memnonian <note>original: "Memnoïnēn," likely referring to Memnon, the mythical Ethiopian king, or a specific Egyptian priestly staff</note> rod <margin>Folio 12 verso</margin> through which you send forth the gods; your name is: Barbariēl; Barbaraiēl; God Barbaraēl; Bēl; Bouēl. Enter, Lord, and answer me through your holy voice, so that I may hear clearly <margin>1035</margin> and truly concerning this matter: <note>vowels and magical words</note> IU EU Ē; Ō Ō A E Ē (formula) IA E Ē; AI A Ē; E AI; EU Ē I E; ŌŌŌŌŌ IU Ē Ō; Jaô; AI.' This is a compulsory prayer. If he should happen to delay, recite this speech following the theology <note>original: "theologia," referring to the divine invocation</note>, saying the words once or three times:

'The great living God commands you, he who exists forever and ever, who shakes all things, <margin>1040</margin> who thunders, who created every soul and race: Jaô AŌI ŌIA AIŌ; IŌA; ŌAÏ. Enter, appear to me, Lord, gracious, kind, gentle, glorious, and without anger, because <margin>1045</margin> I adjure you by the Lord Jaô AŌI ŌIA AIŌ IŌA; ŌAÏ APTA PHŌIRA ZAZOU CHAMĒ. Enter, Lord, appear to me gracious, kind, gentle, glorious, and without anger.'

A greeting to be spoken first when the god has entered. Holding the pebble <note>original: "psēphon," likely a ritual stone used for counting or as a focus</note>, say: 'Hail, Lord, <margin>1050</margin> God of gods, benefactor, Horus, Harpocrates; Alkib, Arsamōsi, Jaô AI; Dagennouth; Raracharai; Abraiaô. Let the Hours <note>the personified goddesses of the times of day</note> greet you, in which you ride your chariot; let the Glories <note>original: "Doxai," personified divine attributes</note> greet you forever, Lord.'

A method for holding the god: When he has entered, after the greeting, press with your left heel upon the big toe of your right foot <margin>1055</margin> and he shall not depart, provided you do not lift your heel from the toe while immediately speaking the dismissal.

Dismissal: Closing your eyes, release the pebble which you are holding, and <margin>1060</margin> taking the wreath from your head and lifting your heel from your toe, say three times with eyes closed: 'I thank you, Lord Bainchoooch <note>A common name for a solar spirit in magical texts</note>, who are Balsamēs. Depart, depart, Lord, to your own heavens, to your own kingdoms, to your own course, keeping me <margin>1065</margin> healthy, unharmed, un-harassed by spirits <note>original: "aneidōloplēkton," literally 'not struck by phantoms'</note>, unstruck, and unafraid, listening to me for the duration of my life.'

Dismissal of the dawn-light: 'CHŌŌ; CHŌŌ; ŌCHŌŌCH; holy dawn' — so that <margin>1070</margin> the light may also depart — 'Depart, holy dawn, depart, good and holy light of the highest god Aiaōna.' Say this once with closed eyes, and smear your eyes with Coptic kohl <note>original: "stimi Koptikon," an Egyptian eye cosmetic</note>, applying it with a golden probe.

A protective charm <term>phylaktērion: a physical object worn to ward off spiritual or physical harm</term> for the ritual, which you must wear for the protection of your whole <margin>1075</margin> body: Take a piece of linen cloth from a stone statue of Harpocrates located in any temple; write upon it with myrrh ink these things: 'I am Horus Alkib; Arsamōsis Jaô AI; Dagennouth; Raracharai Abraiaōth; son of Isis ATHA; BATHA; and of Osiris Osoronnophris <note>original: "Osoron-nōphreōs," the 'Good Being' form of Osiris</note>.' Keep <margin>1080</margin> me healthy, unharmed, un-harassed by spirits, and unafraid for the duration of my life.'

IV 1081—1146

And having placed houseleek <note>original: "aizoön," a plant often used for protection</note> herb inside a rag, roll it up and bind it with 7 Anubian linen threads and wear it around your neck while performing the rite. 
<margin>Folio 13 r.</margin>
**Ritual Procedure:** Taking wide <margin>1086</margin> papyrus ropes, tie them to the four corners of the room so that they form an X; in the middle of the X, tie a small wreath <note>original: "speirion"</note> made of single-stemmed mugwort. 
<margin>1090</margin> Having prepared a wick for a blue-green lamp <note>original: "kallaïnon," a turquoise or sea-green color</note> using the wick-material called *achi* <note>original: "achi," a loanword for marsh grass or sedge</note>, anoint the wick itself with the fat of a black male ram that is first-born and first-reared; and having 
<margin>1095/96</margin> filled the lamp with high-quality oil, place it in the center upon the wreath. Having lit it, stand in the posture previously described, 
<margin>1100</margin> keeping your face toward the East, performing this at all times, being indifferent to the specific days. But maintain purity for 3 days beforehand from all things. Pre-anoint the *achi* <note>marsh grass</note> with the fat of a black male ram, first-born and first-reared. 

**Signs of the Lamp:** After saying the Light-Bringing Invocation, open 
<margin>1105</margin> your eyes and you will see the light of the lamp becoming vault-shaped. Then, with eyes closed, speak (otherwise: [say it] 3 times... after saying it 3 times), and opening them, you will see all things gaping wide and a vast radiance within, while the lamp is nowhere to be seen. You will see the god 
<margin>1110</margin> sitting upon a ciborium <term>ciborium: a canopy-like shrine or pillared throne</term>, radiating light, his right hand raised in greeting, and in his left <insert>holding</insert> a whip, carried by two angels by their hands, and around them are 12 rays.

<margin>1115</margin> ### Hidden Stele
"Hail, the entire system of the aerial spirit, *photaloa*; hail, the spirit that extends from heaven to earth, *erdeneu*, 
<margin>1120</margin> and from the earth in the central hollow of the world unto the depths of the abyss, *meremongga*; hail, the spirit that enters me, and pulls at me, and departs from me according to the will of God in goodness, *ioe Zanophie*; 
<margin>1125</margin> hail, beginning and end of immovable nature, *doryglaophon*; hail, the rotation of the elements' unwearying service, *rogyeu anami pelegeon adara 
<margin>1130</margin> eioph*; hail, the sun-ray’s servant, the illumination of the world, *ieo ueo; iae ai eou oei*; hail, the moon’s night-shining, back-reflecting circle, 
<margin>1135</margin> *aio rema rodouopia*; hail, all you spirits of the aerial phantoms, *romidoue aganasou othaua*; hail, you to whom 'hail' is given in blessing, brothers and sisters, holy men and holy women! O great, greatest, encircling, 
<margin>Bl. 13 v.</margin> inconceivable form of the world! Celestial, *enrocheuel*; heavenly, *peletheu*; ethereal, *iogaraa*; in-the-ether, *thopyleo dardy*; watery, *ioedes*; earthy, *perephia*; fiery, *aphthalua*; windy, *ioie 
<margin>1145</margin> eo aua*; light-like, *alapie*; dark-like, *iepheria*; star-bright, *adamalor*!"

And place the houseleek <note>original: "Hauslauch," a succulent plant often used in ancient folk medicine and magic for protection against lightning and evil spirits</note> plant in the rag, wrap it up and bind it with seven linen Anubis-threads <note>threads named after the Egyptian god of mummification, likely dyed or spun in a ritual manner</note> and wear it around your neck while you are acting. 

**Ritual Procedure:** Take wide ropes made of papyrus <note>original: "Byblos"</note>, bind <margin>1085</margin> them to the four corners of the room so that they form an X. In the center of the X, however, tie a ring woven from single-stemmed wormwood and provide a lamp made of gold-stone <note>The German text says "Goldstein," though the original Greek "kallaïnon" usually refers to a turquoise or blue-green color</note> with a wick made of the so-called *achi* <note>a loanword for Egyptian marsh grass or sedge</note>; and <margin>1090</margin> smear that very wick with the fat of a black, first-born, and first-reared ram. When you have filled the lamp with good oil, set it in the middle of the woven ring and light it, standing there in the <margin>1095</margin> clothing described above, with your face toward the sunrise. You may perform this ritual at any time without choosing specific days; however, keep yourself pure from all things for three days beforehand. Previously, smear the *achi* with the fat of a <margin>1100</margin> black, first-born, and first-reared ram. 

**Sign of the Lamp:** Once you have spoken the light-binding spell (alternatively: after speaking it three times), open your eyes, and you will see the light of the lamp forming itself <margin>1105</margin> like a chamber; then speak with closed eyes (another reading: three times); and when you have opened your eyes, you will see everything widened and a powerful radiance of light within, yet the lamp will be burning nowhere. You will see the God sitting on a *kiborion* <note>a vaulted canopy or throne-structure</note>, provided with rays, stretching <margin>1110</margin> his right hand up in greeting, holding a whip in his left, carried by two angels with their hands, and around them in a circle are 12 rays.

O great, <margin>1135</margin> greatest, circular, incomprehensible form of the world! <margin>1275</margin> # The Ritual of the Bear that accomplishes all.
The prayer: 'I invoke you, the greatest power in heaven <note>The "Bear" refers to Ursa Major, which in ancient magic was seen as the celestial pivot that turned the universe.</note> (others say: the power in the Bear) appointed by the Lord God to <margin>1280</margin> turn the sacred pole with a mighty hand, *nikaroplēx* <note>original: νικαροπληξ; a magical word of power</note>; harken to me, Sun-God Phre <note>Phre is the Greek rendering of the Egyptian Sun God, Ra (Pi-Re)</note>, hear the sacred <insert>word</insert>, you who hold the universe together and give life to the whole world, <margin>1285</margin> *thōzopithē euchandama ōchrienther omnyōdēs chēmiochynēs ieōy* (offer incense) *thermouther psiphirix* <margin>Leaf 15 r.</margin> *phrosali kanthimeu zenzemia hyper peromenēs rōthieu ēnin-deu korkountho eumen menikēdeua* <margin>1291</margin> *kēpsēoi*.' The general part. A request addressed to the Sun at sunset. The prayer: 'Thēnōr <note>Hebrew: "Giver of Light"</note> Sun-God Santhēnōr, I call upon you, Lord; let the place of the Bear and its lord be available to me.' And <margin>1295</margin> offer incense while making the request for *armara* <note>possibly a specific type of aromatic resin</note>; do this toward the setting sun. Compulsory for the third day: '*anteberyrtōr erementhechōr chnychiroantōr meneloechyr; hēssipo* giver of grace *gou pi* <margin>1300</margin> protection *ōmalamingor mantatoncha*, perform such-and-such a deed.' Alternatively, the first prayer: 'Thōzopithē, Bear, greatest goddess, ruler of heaven, queen of the starry pole, highest, fair-shining goddess, indestructible element, system of the universe, <margin>1305</margin> all-bright, harmony of the whole *a e ē i o y ō* (the square) <note>original: πλινθίον; this indicates a "vowel square," a magical grid where the seven Greek vowels are arranged in a block</note>, you who are stationed at the pole, whom the Lord God appointed to turn the sacred pole with a mighty hand; *thōzopithē* (the word).' Incense for the ritual: 4 drachmas <note>A drachma was a unit of weight roughly equivalent to 4 grams</note> of frankincense, 4 drachmas of myrrh, 2 ounces each of cassia leaf and white pepper, <margin>1310</margin> 1 drachma of bdellium <note>a fragrant resin similar to myrrh</note>, 1 drachma of asphodel seed, 2 drachmas each of amomum, saffron, and turpentine-storax, 1 drachma of mugwort, herb of compulsion [...], priestly *kyphi* <note>a complex Egyptian temple incense</note>, and the whole brain of a black ram. <margin>1315</margin> Take this up with white Mendesian wine <note>Wine from the Mendesian region of the Nile Delta, prized in antiquity</note> and honey and make pills. Protective charm for the ritual: Wear the ankle bone of a wolf as an amulet, and mix into the <margin>1320</margin> censer the juice of the compulsion-herb and pondweed; write this name in the middle of the censer: '*thermoutherepsiphiripisali*' (24 letters), and offer incense in this way. Another: '*komphtho komasith komnoun*, you who have shaken and continue to shake the inhabited world, who <margin>1325</margin> swallowed the ever-living serpent and who daily lift up the disk of the sun and the moon, whose name is *ithiōō ēï Arbathiaōth ē*, send up to me, [Name], <margin>1330</margin> during the night, the demon of this night to give me information concerning such-and-such a matter.'

### All-working Power of the Bear Constellation. <margin>1275</margin>
The prayer: "I invoke you, the greatest power in heaven <note>The "Bear" refers to Ursa Major, which ancient practitioners viewed as the celestial engine that turned the heavens.</note> (others say: in the Bear constellation), appointed by God the Lord to turn the holy pole with a strong hand <note>original: ZW (Zauberworte); indicates magical words of power</note>: harken to me, <margin>1280</margin> holy (prayer), Helios Phre <note>Phre is the Greek form of the Egyptian Sun-God, Ra-Pi</note>, who holds the universe together and animates the entire world (Thôzopithê-Logos <note>A specific sequence of magical names</note>)." Burn incense. "(words of power, at your discretion)." Petitioning, toward the sun, <margin>1290</margin> toward the sunset. Prayer: "(words of power) Helios (words of power), I ask, Lord: let the place and lord of the Bear constellation have time for me!" And burn incense during the petitioning of Armara <note>A name or a specific aromatic</note>; perform the action toward sunset. Compulsion formula of the <margin>1295</margin> third day: "(words of power, including 'Giver' and 'Watchman'), do the thing in question." The <margin>1300</margin> first prayer in another version: "(Thôzopithê) Arktos, greatest goddess, who rules the heavens, governs the stars of the pole, highest, beautifully-shining goddess, imperishable constellation, bond of the universe, all-illuminating, harmony of the <margin>1305</margin> entire (planets) *aeēiouō* <note>The seven Greek vowels representing the celestial spheres, often arranged in a magical square</note>, standing upon the pole, whom God the Lord appointed to turn the holy pole with a strong hand (Thôzopithê-Logos)." Incense offering for the ritual: 4 drachmas of frankincense, 4 drachmas of myrrh, cassia-laurel leaf, 2 ounces each of white pepper, 1 drachma of bdellium resin, 1 drachma of asphodel <margin>1310</margin> seeds, amomum, saffron, 2 drachmas of turpentine-styrax, 1 drachma of mugwort, of the plant Katanankê <note>literally "compulsion-plant," likely Blue Cupidone</note> [...], hieratic kyphi <note>A sacred incense used in Egyptian temples</note>, the whole brain of a black ram. Mix it with white Mendesian wine and <margin>1315</margin> honey and make it into a dough. Protection for the ritual: bind a wolf’s knucklebone <note>The astragalus or "knucklebone" of a wolf was a common protective amulet</note> around yourself and add juice of Katanankê and Potamogeitôn <note>pondweed</note> to the incense burner; write this name in the center of the incense burner: (words of power, 24 <margin>1320</margin> letters) and thus burn the incense. Another reading: "(words of power) who has shaken and shakes the earth, who has swallowed the ever-living serpent and daily <margin>1325</margin> destroys the circle of the sun and the moon, whose name is (words of power), send me, [Name], by night the demon of this night, to prophesy to me about the <margin>1330</margin> matter in question."

**Attraction spell by means of heroes, or gladiators, or those who died by violence.**

# IV 1844—1927

<margin>1845</margin> [The figurine should be] wearing a cloak, having the right foot thrust forward, and having a hollow back. Into the hollow, <margin>Bl. 21 v. 1850</margin> place a gold leaf after writing with a cold-forged copper stylus the name: **Marsaboutarthe** <note>original: Μαρσαβουταρθε; a powerful magical name frequently found in these papyri</note>. [Say:] "Become for me a companion, a helper, and a sender of dreams." And going late in the evening to the house of whichever woman you wish, knock on her door <margin>1855</margin> with the [figurine of] Eros and say: "See, here dwells [name], so that you, standing beside her, may say what I intend, having taken the form of the god or spirit she worships." And having returned to your own <margin>1860</margin> house, set a table and, after spreading a clean linen cloth and seasonal flowers, <margin>1865</margin> place the figurine upon it. Then offer incense to it and say the words of the invocation continuously and send [the spirit], and he will act without fail. And whenever you go to bed with the [engraved] stone, on that <margin>1870</margin> night he sends the dream; for one thing follows another.

. . . . Teach no one. For this is exceedingly powerful and unsurpassed, acting <margin>1875</margin> upon everyone on the very same day—simply a most powerful and disciplined [rite]. It is this: taking 4 ounces of wax, 8 ounces of vitex fruit <note>term: vitex (Greek: agnos); a plant associated with chastity and ritual purity</note>, and 4 drachmas of manna. <margin>1880</margin> Having ground each of these separately, mix them with pitch and wax and fashion a dog eight fingers <margin>1885</margin> high, with a gaping mouth. You shall place into the mouth of the dog a bone from the head of a man who died a violent death, and write upon the ribs of the dog <margin>1890</margin> these characters: **ΧΖΟΠ ⎓ Ψ VΨ**. And you shall place the dog upon a tripod. Let <margin>1895</margin> the dog have its right foot raised. And write upon a small slip of paper these <margin>Bl. 22 r. 1900</margin> names and whatever you desire: "Iao asto iophe" <note>original: Ἰάω αστω ιωφη; Iao is a Greek rendering of the Hebrew name for God, Yahweh</note>, and you shall place the paper on the tripod, and stand the dog upon the paper. And <margin>1905</margin> say these names many times. And as you say the words, the dog hisses. And if it should hiss, she is not coming. Therefore, speak the words again, and if it should bark, it brings [her]. Then, having opened the door, you will find at the doors the woman you desire. Let a censer be placed <margin>1910</margin> beside the dog, in which frankincense is placed, while saying the formula.

The formula: "Barking-dog <note>original: baukyon (βαυκύων); likely an onomatopoeic name for a barking spirit</note>, I adjure you, Cerberus <note>The multi-headed hound of the Underworld</note>, by those who have been snatched away and the dead and those who <margin>1915</margin> died by violence: bring to me [name], daughter of [mother's name], to me, [your name], son of [mother's name]. I adjure you, Cerberus, by the sacred head of the subterranean gods: lead to me [name], <margin>1920</margin> daughter of [mother's name]—**zouch zouki to pary hyphibarmo enor sekemi kriphoudasephi tribepsi** <note>magical sounds or "voces magicae" intended to compel the spirits</note>—lead <margin>1925</margin> to me [name], daughter of [mother's name], to me, [your name], already, already, quickly, quickly." You shall also say the "general-purpose" formula. You shall do these things on level ground, in a clean place.

And then go into your house, set a table, and spread a clean linen <margin>1860</margin> cloth with seasonal flowers and place the figurine upon it; then offer incense to it and speak the prayer of invocation without interruption and send it, and it <margin>1865</margin> will carry it out exactly. For sometimes one relies on one <margin>1870</margin> [method], and sometimes on the other.

. . . Let no one know of this. For it is very powerful and unsurpassed, as it works against anyone on the very same day, absolutely without delay, <margin>1875</margin> exceedingly powerful. It consists of this: take <pitch and wax> 4 ounces, fruit of the chaste-tree <note>term: Keuschbaum (Latin: Vitex agnus-castus); a plant used in antiquity to manage sexual desire and maintain ritual purity</note> 8 ounces, and manna 4 drachmae. And if it growls, she is not coming. Therefore, speak the prayer again, and if it barks, it is bringing her here. <margin>1905</margin> Then open the door, and you will find at the entrance the one you desire. Beside the dog, let there be an incense-altar on which frankincense must lie <margin>1910</margin> when you speak the prayer. Prayer: "Barking dog, I conjure you, Cerberus <note>The three-headed hound of the Underworld</note>, by those who have been hanged and the dead and those who have died a violent death: lead to <margin>1915</margin> me [Name], the daughter of [Mother's Name], to me, [Name], the son of [Mother's Name]. I conjure you, Cerberus, by the sacred head of the subterranean gods: lead to me [Name], the daughter of [Mother's Name] (Magical Formula). Lead to me [Name], the daughter of [Mother's Name], <margin>1920</margin> to me, [Name], now, now, quickly, quickly!" Speak also the all-working <margin>1925</margin> formula. Perform this on the ground floor, in a clean place.

<margin>2070</margin> The <term>magical figure</term> <note>original: zoidion; a symbolic image or character used to focus ritual power</note> to be indicated—circle it with this spoken formula and place it beneath him, and he will bring [the target] immediately; and if the person is unyielding, [the spirit brings them] without delay, not exceeding a single day. Often, there will be no need for the <term>cotton leaf</term> <note>original: kalpassos; likely the leaf of the cotton plant, though sometimes interpreted as a specific fine-fiber herb</note>, but the <margin>2075</margin> <term>magic tablet</term> <note>original: pittakion; a small slip of papyrus or skin inscribed with a spell</note> shall be placed in a second [vessel] once you have commanded it to serve you. This procedure brings [people], causes <term>catalepsy</term> <note>original: kataklinei; literally "to lay someone down," often referring to a spell causing illness or binding someone to their bed</note>, sends dreams, restrains [enemies], and requests dreams all at once. These are the things that this <margin>2080</margin> single procedure accomplishes. Regarding the performance, change only the <term>common instructions</term> <note>original: koinologias; the standard parts of a spell where the user inserts specific names or desires</note>. Most magicians, having carried the ritual vessels with them and set them down, have used this <term>divine assistant</term> <note>original: paredros; a supernatural helper or familiar spirit bound to the magician</note> and have accomplished the tasks before them with all speed. For he is <margin>2085</margin> without any idle talk, performing the tasks set before him immediately with the greatest ease.

<sig>Folio 24 recto</sig>

**The Spoken Formula:**
“I say to you, <term>underworld spirit</term> <note>original: katachthonios daimon; a spirit residing in the realm of the dead or beneath the earth</note>, <margin>2090</margin> whose essence was embodied in this [man or woman] on this very night: Go to where [she or he] dwells, and bring her to me, ‘So-and-so’ (insert your name), either in the middle of the night or with speed. Perform this specific task, for it is the holy god <margin>2095</margin> **Osiris Kmephis** <note>Kmephis is a Greek rendering of an Egyptian name for a creator-god, often depicted as a serpent or a primordial form of Osiris/Amun</note> who wills this and commands you. Accomplish, O spirit, the things written here. When you have accomplished them, I will give you a sacrifice; but if you delay, I will bring punishments upon you which you cannot endure. Accomplish this specific task for me, now, now! Quick, quick!”

<margin>2100</margin> These are the inks for this procedure:
The <term>membrane</term> <note>original: hymen; usually referring to a prepared animal skin or parchment</note> is inscribed with the blood of a donkey, from the heart of one that has been slaughtered, with which <term>blacksmith’s soot</term> is mixed. 
<margin>2105</margin> The <term>cotton leaf</term> is inscribed with hawk’s blood, with which <term>goldsmith’s soot</term> is mixed. 
The <term>priestly papyrus</term> <note>original: hieratikos chartes; a high-quality grade of papyrus used for sacred texts</note> is inscribed with eel’s blood, with which <term>acacia</term> is mixed.
Perform these things in this way, and having completed them, you may know the great power this ritual arrangement possesses in its ease, <margin>2110</margin> considering the vessels themselves to be the assistant. But guard yourself with whatever protection you wish.

The <term>magical figure</term> to be drawn on the membrane is: a lion-faced statue, girdled, <margin>2115</margin> holding a staff in its right hand upon which there is a serpent; in its left hand, let an entire asp be coiled; and let fire breathe out from the lion’s mouth.

The figure for the <margin>2120</margin> cotton leaf is this: **Hecate** <note>The goddess of magic, crossroads, and the underworld, often depicted in triple form</note> with three faces and six hands, holding torches in her hands. On the right side of her face she has the head of a cow, on the left the head of a dog, and in the middle the head of a maiden, and she is wearing sandals.

<margin>2125</margin> The figure for the papyrus: **Osiris** dressed in robes, as the Egyptians indicate.

**A Binding Seal:**
Against the <term>inharmonious sounds</term> <note>original: akatallēlous; perhaps referring to the rattling or discordant noises made by the vessels during the rite</note> of the cups; further, you must not speak at all while doing these things. Seal the mouth of the cup with <term>refuse</term> <note>original: rypou; likely ritual grime or a specific sealing substance like wax mixed with soot</note>...

### IV 2183—2246

...you by the gods of the underworld <note>original: "ZW" / "Zauberwort"; a placeholder for a secret magic word</note>: serve me in whatever I call you for." <margin>2185</margin> Speak the all-working formula. 

**Consecration of the little tablet:** Go into a clean room, set up a table upon which should be a clean linen cloth and flowers of the season, and sacrifice a white rooster. Beside it <margin>2190</margin> should lie 7 offering cakes, 7 wide breads, and 7 lamps. Pour a libation of milk, honey, wine, and oil. The prayer that is spoken during the consecration of the tablet is as follows: 

"Come to me, Lord, who commands above the earth and under the earth, <margin>2195</margin> who looks toward the West and the East, and gazes toward the South and the North, Lord of the All, Aeon of Aeons <note>original: "Aiôn der Aiône"; refers to the personification of eternal time</note>. You are the Ruler of the World, Ra, Pan <note>The scribe invokes Ra, the Egyptian sun god, and Pan, the Greek god of nature, as universal forces</note> (Magic <margin>2200</margin> word, vowel sequence), Baubo Baubo, Phorba Phorba <note>Names associated with Hecate and the underworld</note>, who hunts while striding across the mountains (vowels)." 

But speak the formula of Necessity <note>original: "Anankê"; the personification of fate or compulsion</note>: the Maskelli-Logos <note>A famous long string of magical syllables used for protection and authority</note>, (Magic Word), <margin>2205</margin> and the formula that works for everything. That is the consecration; the actions follow.

**For a revelation:** write on a laurel leaf with myrrh and the blood of one who died a violent death <note>original: "gewaltsam Gestorbenen"; spirits of those who died violently were believed to be more active in the human world</note>, and lay it under the tablet: "Abraa, you are the one who <margin>2210</margin> foretells all (Magic Word)." 

**To crash racing chariots:** burn as incense a single-clove garlic and the old skin of a snake, and write on a tin tablet: "(Magic Word with 'Neboutosoualêth', 'Erbêth', 'Pakerbêth' <note>These are names associated with the god Seth-Typhon, often invoked in aggressive magic</note>). Overthrow N.N. <note>A placeholder for the name of the intended victim</note> and those who are with him." Bury the tablet in the grave of one who died prematurely <margin>2215</margin> <note>original: "vorzeitig Gestorbenen"; like the violently dead, these spirits were thought to be restless and easily commanded</note> for three days: for as long as you have laid it there, he will work by day. 

**For binding spells:** write on a sea shell with the ink mentioned below, to which you have mixed Typhon's red lead <margin>2220</margin> <note>original: "Typhônsmennig"; minium or cinnabar, associated with the red-haired god Seth-Typhon</note>, and bury it in the grave of one who died prematurely when the Moon is exactly opposite the Sun. The accompanying inscription consists of the three verses, and below them: "Io Bolchoseth, Iakoub <note>A magical combination of the god Seth and the biblical Jacob</note> (Magic Word), Erbeth, Io Pakerbeth." But let the tablet be hung up, as <margin>2225</margin> in the first cases. 

**To acquire favor and for love magic:** write on a little gold tablet: (Magic Word). But first lay it for 3 days under the iron one, <margin>2230</margin> then take it and wear it in purity. 

**For compulsory love spells:** burn rose and sumac as incense, take myrrh leaves and write on them with ink: "(Magic Word, vowels) Lead N.N. to N.N." And recite the formula <margin>2235</margin> and place her personal magical material <note>original: "Zauberstoff"; likely hair or a piece of clothing from the target</note> under (the tablet). But add to the myrrh ink some (juice) of single-stemmed wormwood. But hang the tablet on a cord that you have taken from the place where the wool-workers work. <margin>2240</margin>

**Averting inscription to Selênê.** <note>Selênê is the personification of the Moon</note> Prayer: "Hail, holy light, Mistress of Tartarus <note>The deepest abyss of the underworld</note>, you who strike with light; hail, holy radiance of light, who was taken from the darkness, you who throw everything into confusion with reckless counsel: I will call upon you, and you shall hear my holy prayers; for... <margin>2245</margin>

<note>The following are philological notes regarding the Greek manuscript:</note>

Magic word from the *Pistis Sophia* <note>A significant Gnostic text</note> 271 (Schmidt); similarly, "shining" and "elzate" are found there. "Hêmerê" <note>Day</note> appears in the manuscript; perhaps "Himerê" as a feminine form of *Himeros* <note>Desire</note>? 2283: "liggeia" could be "ligeia" <note>clear-toned</note> or "lygkeia" <note>lynx-like</note>. 2284: "With shining locks"; the letter 'e' is blurred in the manuscript. See Orphic Hymn 36, 11: "beautiful sprout" (referring to Artemis). 2285: "Theban patient one," perhaps referring to Semele or Antiope. 2287: "Full of guile" (compare with Psalm 9:28). 2289: Compare with lines 2999 and 2330. 2291: Brimo: "Calling Brimo-Hecate, helper in the contests" (Apollonius of Rhodes 3, 1211). "Sachmi" is certainly the goddess Sekhmet; see the Egyptian name Petesachmis in the Petrie Papyri. 2294: The manuscript mentions "Cerberus of Tartarus"; some scholars suggest deleting "Tartarus" for meter.
