<note>Scholarly Apparatus Translation:</note>
Compare to the *Greek Anthology* appendix 335, 2: "of the holy Nilotic goddess Isis." Jacoby, *Byzantine-Neo-Greek Yearbooks* 3, 420. 
**Line 2298:** The papyrus reads "henidousa." Preisendanz reads "look upon me by the grace of the Nilotic one, a mirror in which seeing yourself you will marvel." Kunze interprets: "Look at me by the grace of Isis; looking into the mirror you will see yourself to be Isis."
**Line 2299:** Jacoby thinks of the myth of Horus and Ra (the motif of spitting in magic).
**Lines 2301/11:** Hopfner, *Oriental Religious Texts* 1 § 403. A similar invocation is found in PGM VII 780—787. In the papyrus, a colon is placed between individual words.
**Line 2306:** On "Pan’s offspring," see Gruppe, *Greek Mythology* 944, 4.
**Line 2307:** The papyrus reads "chamailykon nethousa" (spinning ground-wolf). Wessely suggests "blooming chameleon"; Hercher and Hopfner suggest "chamailykos." K. suggests "nethousa" might be the spindle tree.
**Line 2308:** "Aris" is a type of plant in Hesychius; Wünsch suggests "a borer." For the "gray-eyed woman," Wessely and Preisendanz agree; Hercher and Kunze read "gray/bright." The color is also named for the "Sphinx" in line 2309. This may refer to a person of color.
**Line 2309:** Sphinx: "apes (sphinges), hairy with hair, with breasts somewhat prominent and deep, teachable to the point of forgetting their wildness" (Solinus 27).
**Line 2310:** The papyrus reads "theoroumene" (being seen); Wessely suggests "peroumene" (maimed/blinded); Eitrem suggests "toroumene" (pierced/carved).
**Lines 2311 f.:** Compare PGM XIII 19, 41 f. Hercher translates: "the whole world will be confused for me." Kunze notes "pneuma" (spirit) refers to "magical power."
**Line 2313:** Papyrus has "nyton," corrected to "noton" (South).
**Line 2317:** Papyrus has "eisaden," corrected to "eis Haiden" (into Hades).
**Line 2322:** The papyrus has "odeise," with "se" likely intruding from line 2299. For "saten," Wessely reads "s' aten" (your ruin) and Kunze reads "t' Aten" (and Ate/Ruin). Wünsch and Eitrem read "sautēn" (yourself).
**Line 2324:** The papyrus uses "deina" (so-and-so/placeholder); Preisendanz reads "dei" (it is necessary).
**Line 2330:** Regarding the "leader of the gods," see line 2289, where the magician identifies himself as Hermes. Wessely and others read "tomorrow does not happen, it must happen now."

# IV 2346—2418

->The earth drinks the dew and conceives, from which the world increases and is sustained.<-

<margin>2350</margin> *Euphorbia phorba; phorboreou; phorba phorbôr phorbôr phorbôr; borborpha; êrphor; phorbaiô; phorbôr phorbôr boroph; phorphor bor; phorbôr; au; iôê; phorborphor; euphorphophor; euoieu phôth; iôphôth iôphôth phôthiôph; auôôthô ôai iô eôôi* <note>These "voces magicae" (magical words) are rhythmic, chant-like sounds intended to vibrate with cosmic power; "Euphorbia" may refer to the spurge plant or a mythical name.</note>

<margin>2355</margin> *uuuuu aeêiouu uuu* <note>The seven Greek vowels representing the seven planets.</note> "Queen, Arkentechtha <note>A magical name for a goddess, likely Hecate or Isis</note>, the god who appears alongside the Lord Osiris, fulfill this for me, Michael, archangel of angels!"

<margin>2360</margin> **A Business Ritual:** Taking yellow wax and the juices of the "airy" plant <note>original: "aerias"; possibly a plant like pellitory-of-the-wall or an unidentified herb</note> and moonwort <note>original: "selenitis"</note>, mix them and fashion a hollow figure of Hermes. In his left hand, let him hold a caduceus <note>the traditional herald's staff of Hermes</note> and in his right, a small money-bag. Write upon hieratic papyrus <note>a high-quality grade of papyrus used by priests</note> these names, and you shall see <margin>2365</margin> unceasing [results]: "Chaiôchen outibilmemnouôth; atrauich; give profit and business to this place, for Psentebeth <note>possibly meaning "Son of the Falcon" in Demotic Egyptian</note> dwells here." And having inserted the papyrus, seal it up again with the same wax. <margin>2370</margin> Place it inside a wall, hidden from view, and crown it on the outside. Offer to him a rooster as a burnt offering, having poured a libation of Egyptian wine, and burn for him a lamp that has not been colored with red earth <note>original: "amiltôton"; a pure, plain clay lamp</note>.

**A ritual for success and summoning for a workshop, a house, or wherever you may** <margin>2375</margin> **establish it:** Having this, you will grow wealthy and you will succeed; for Hermes did this for Isis when she was wandering <note>a reference to the myth of Isis searching for the pieces of Osiris</note>. It is truly marvelous and is called the "Beggar's Tool" <note>original: "epaitetarion"</note>. Taking <margin>2380</margin> unrefined wax, called bee-glue <term>propolis: a resinous mixture honeybees produce</term>, fashion a man with his right hand held out to beg and a pouch and a staff in his left. Let there be a serpent coiled around the staff, and let the man himself be in a loincloth, standing upon a sphere <margin>2385</margin> that also has a serpent coiled around it, just like Isis. You shall set it up by fixing it to a base of juniper wood, having a carved figure of Thermouthis <note>the Egyptian cobra goddess of the harvest and protection</note> and a basket hidden on top. Fashion him <margin>Bl. 27 r.</margin> on a god's New Moon <note>the beginning of the lunar month</note> and perform the rite while rejoicing. Read the formula over his limbs <margin>2390</margin> four times, standing a short distance away from him. When you <margin>2395</margin> elevate it in the place you choose, sacrifice a "white-browed" wild ass <note>original: "onagrios"</note>, and having made a whole burnt offering, inspect the entrails. After roasting them over willow wood, eat them. These are the things written on each slip:

### IV 2476—2528

...the slander <note>original: "diabolē" — a common magical technique where the magician tells a god that the victim has insulted them, hoping to provoke the deity's wrath against that person.</note> of the filthy and unholy woman, so-and-so: "For she has betrayed your sacred mysteries to men for their knowledge. She is the one who said—it was not I—who said: 'I saw the greatest <margin>2480</margin> goddess leaving the heavenly pole, walking the earth barefoot, sword-bearing, and speaking an unspeakable name.' She is the one who said: <margin>2485</margin> 'I saw the goddess drinking blood.'" She said it, not I: "Aktiōphi, Ereschigal <note>Ereschigal is the Sumerian queen of the underworld; here she is syncretized with Hekate.</note>, Neboutosoualēth, Phorphorba, Satrapammōn, Choirieie, Eater of Flesh! Walk to so-and-so and take away her sleep; give her a burning of the soul <note>original: "psychē" — in this context, it may refer to the "nature" or even the genitals, implying sexual arousal.</note>, punishment of the mind, <margin>Bl. 28r.</margin> and madness. Drive her out from every place and every house and lead her here, to me, so-and-so." After saying these things, offer the sacrifice; then, groaning, <margin>2495</margin> go down walking backward, and she will come immediately. But keep a watch for the one who is being led, so that you may open the door for her; otherwise, she will die.

For making someone lie down <note>original: "kataklisis" — a spell to make someone fall ill or take to their bed.</note>, use these words, adding: "Make so-and-so, whom so-and-so bore, lie down." But for a killing <note>original: "anairesis" — a lethal curse.</note>, say: "Lady, draw up the <margin>2500</margin> breath from the nostrils of so-and-so." For sending dreams, say: "Take the form of the god she worships." For a requested dream <note>original: "oneiraitētos" — a spell to receive information in a dream.</note>, say: "Stand beside me, Lady, and give me a revelation concerning such-and-such a matter." And she will stand beside you and <margin>2505</margin> tell you everything truthfully. 

Do not perform this lightly unless you have a great necessity. It also requires a protective amulet <term>phylaktērion (a physical object or text worn for protection)</term> to prevent you from being struck down; for the goddess is accustomed to making those who perform this without protection "air-borne" <note>original: "aerophereis" — likely meaning being physically lifted or thrown by spirits.</note> and casting them from the height to the <margin>2510</margin> ground. Therefore, I considered it necessary to take care regarding the amulet as well, so that you may act without hesitation. Keep this secret! Take a strip of priestly papyrus <note>original: "hieratikon kollēma" — high-quality papyrus used by the temple elite.</note> and wear it <margin>2515</margin> around your right arm, while you offer the incense. These are the things to be written: "Moulathi, Chernouth, Amarō, Moulianndron. Protect me from every evil spirit, whether male or female." Keep this secret, my son!

The second formula to be spoken after <margin>2520</margin> you have sacrificed first; however, it is better to say it before you offer the incense. It is a formula to be joined with the first: "I offer to you this incense, Child of Zeus, Showerer of Arrows, Artemis, Persephone, Shooter of Deer, Appearing by Night, Three-clanging, <margin>2525</margin> Three-voiced, Three-headed Selene, Three-pronged, Three-faced, Three-necked, and Goddess of the Three-way Crossroads, who hold the unwearied fire of flame in three baskets, and you who haunt the triple crossroads and rule over the triple decades..."

### IV 2476—2528

...through the criminal and impious so-and-so <note>N.N. stands for "nomen nominandum," where the magician would insert the specific name of the victim.</note>: for she has spoken slanderously of your holy mysteries, making them known to men. It is so-and-so who said it—it was not I who spoke so: <margin>2480</margin>
> "I saw the greatest goddess leaving the heavenly vault and walking the earth barefoot, carrying a sword, and calling out an unseemly name."

It is so-and-so who said:
> "I saw <the goddess> drinking blood."

So-and-so spoke thus, not I; <note>The text here contains magic words: Aktiōphi, Ereschigal, Neboutosoualēth, Phorphorba, Satrapammōn, Choirieie.</note> <margin>2485</margin> "Ereschigal, Neboutosoualeth, Ruler Ammon, Eater of Flesh," go to so-and-so and take the sleep from her and give her a burning of her nature <note>original: "Brand der Natur" — referring to intense sexual fever or a "fire in the loins."</note>, punishment of her senses, and raging passion, and drive her from every place and every house and <margin>2490</margin> lead her here to me, so-and-so. After these words, offer the sacrifice and cry out loudly and go back downstairs walking backwards, and she will come immediately: but watch out for the one who has been summoned, that you open the door for her; otherwise she will die. <margin>2495</margin> To cause illness <note>original: "kataklisis" — a spell to make someone bedridden.</note>, use these prayers as well and add: "Throw so-and-so, daughter of so-and-so, onto her bed." But for the purpose of destruction <note>original: "Beseitigung" — likely a spell for the "removal" of life or breath.</note>, say: "Draw the breath, Mistress, from the nose of so-and-so!" <margin>2500</margin> And for sending dreams (add): "Make yourself like the deity to whom she prays." For a dream request, however, say: "Come to me, Mistress, and reveal to me concerning the matter at hand." And she will approach you and say everything without deceit. Do not act lightly with this, but only when a necessity <margin>2505</margin> presents itself to you. There is a protective charm that keeps you from falling; for the goddess is accustomed to leading those who act without protection high into the air and hurling them from the height to the earth. Therefore, I considered it necessary to take care for the protective charm, so that you may act <margin>2510</margin> safely. Keep it secret. Take a sheet glued from hieratic paper <note>High-quality papyrus used by priests.</note> and wear it around your right arm while you incense. Its inscription <margin>2515</margin> is this: <note>Magic words follow: "ASKEI KATASKEI ERŌN OREŌN IŌR MEGA SAMNYÊR..."</note> "Protect me from every evil demon, whether a male or female wicked spirit." **Equipment for the protection of the procedure:**
Take a "breathing" magnet <term>breathing magnet</term> <note>original: μάγνητα τὸν πνέοντα. This refers to a "living" or "spirited" lodestone, believed to possess natural magical power.</note> and shape it into a heart. Let Hekate be engraved upon it, surrounded by the heart as if by crescent moons. <margin>2635</margin> Then, engrave the twenty-letter vowel-name and wear it upon your body. This is the name to be written below: "aeuu ēie· oa· eōē· eua· ōi· eui." <margin>2640</margin> For this word is capable of accomplishing everything. Do this with purity, however; do not do it frequently <margin>Bl. 29v.</margin> or carelessly, especially in the presence of the Moon.

...in your own dream; it eliminates enemies, depending on how you alter the prayer, just as you wish. But provide yourself above all with a protective charm and do not approach <margin>2630</margin> the practice carelessly; otherwise, the goddess will be enraged.

### Preparation of the protective charm for the magic:
Take a "breathing" magnet <term>breathing magnet</term> <note>original German: "den atmenden"; Greek: "pneonta". This refers to a "living" lodestone or natural magnet, believed to possess an active spiritual force.</note> and shape it like a heart. Let an image of Hekate be carved upon it, surrounded by the heart as if by <margin>2635</margin> a small crescent moon. Then, scratch in the twenty-letter name made of vowels and wear it on your body. The following name is the inscription: (20 Vowels). For this formula, when executed in this way, accomplishes everything. 

Perform this in a state of purity, of course, and by no means <margin>2640</margin> frequently or with indifference toward Selene <note>The personification of the Moon</note>. It is best to burn Cretan resin on juniper wood and begin with the prayer. The prayer that you speak: 

"N.N. <note>The practitioner inserts the name of the victim here</note> burns for you, Goddess, a hateful sacrificial offering: the fat <margin>2645</margin> and blood and filth of a dappled goat, the embryo of a dog, and the discharge <term>ichor</term> <note>original: "Blutwasser". In Greek magic, this refers to the decomposed fluids of a corpse.</note> of a virgin who died before her time, and the heart of a young boy mixed with <margin>2650</margin> bran and vinegar, salt, and a deer’s antler, and sea-onion, and myrrh, and dark laurel, recklessly, and the claws of a crab, yellow sage, a rose, a fruit pit for you, and garlic without side-shoots, and onion, and the filth of a shrew, the blood of a baboon <term>cynocephalus</term> <note>original: "Hundskopfaffe". A dog-headed baboon, sacred to Thoth in Egypt and often appearing in these Greco-Egyptian spells.</note>, and the egg of a young ibis; <margin>2654</margin> she laid these—what an abomination!—upon your altar of juniper wood. 

The woman N.N. <margin>2655</margin> has claimed that *you* performed this deed: she said that you killed a human being and drank his blood, that you ate his flesh, that his intestines are your headband, she says, and that you took his whole skin and placed it upon your genitals; <note>The magician is accusing the victim of slandering the goddess with these gruesome images</note> you drink the blood of a sea-hawk, and your <margin>2660</margin> food is the dung beetle. Pan <note>The goat-legged god of the wild</note> has discharged his wicked seed against your face, and from this the baboon is born during the whole time of your monthly purification. 

But you, Ruler Aktiophis <note>A secret magical name for the Moon-Goddess</note>, only Mistress, <margin>2665</margin> Selene, Fate of gods and demons (Magic Words: [ZW], or alternatively: [ZW]), provide bitter punishments for N.N., the wicked one, whom I will in turn <margin>2670</margin> convict of being your enemy (here add at your discretion, in ordinary speech, whatever wicked things she speaks against the gods). For otherwise, she will use her prayer to force even the rocks to burst."

### IV 2790—2855

Born one, sitting upon wild-glancing bulls, Queen who travels on the same path as the Sun <note>original: "Helios"</note> in a chariot, you who dance in the three forms of the three Graces <note>The Charites: Aglaia, Euphrosyne, and Thalia</note>, reveling with the stars, <margin>2795</margin> you are Justice <note>original: "Dike"</note> and the threads of the Fates <note>original: "Moirae"</note>: you are Clotho, Lachesis, and Atropos. You are the three-headed one, Persephone, Megaera, and Alecto <note>Megaera and Alecto are Furies, spirits of divine vengeance</note>. O many-formed goddess, who arms her hands with dark and terrible torches, who <margin>2800</margin> shakes a mane of frightening snakes at her brow, who sends forth the bellowing of bulls from her mouths, whose body is covered with snake-scales, with venom-sending <margin>2805</margin> coils of serpents upon her shoulders, bound across the back under the force of the most gruesome magical bonds. 

You who call out in the night, bull-faced, lover of solitude, bull-headed: your eye looks like a bull's eye, you have the voice <margin>2810</margin> of dogs, you protect the forms of lions at your calves, your ankle resembles that of a wolf, and savage-hearted dogs are dear to you; therefore they call you Hekate, O goddess of many names. You are the Moon <note>original: "Mene"</note>, cutting through the air, appearing as the arrow-shooting <margin>2815</margin> Artemis. 

Four-faced goddess, four-named goddess of the four-way crossroads, Artemis, Persephone, deer-slayer, shining by night, triple-stomping, calling <margin>2820</margin> from a triple mouth, three-headed, three-named Selene <note>The Moon goddess</note>, you with the three-pronged winnowing fan, three-faced, three-necked goddess of the triple-way, who holds the tireless fire of the flame in a triple torch and <margin>2825</margin> rules the triple-ways and commands the three decades of nights <note>referring to the thirty days of the lunar month</note>. 

Be gracious to me who calls upon you, and hear me kindly, you who rule over the wide-encompassing world by night, before whom the demons shudder and the immortals <margin>2830</margin> tremble. Goddess who glorifies men, many-named, beautifully born, bull-eyed, horned, producer of gods and men and Nature, the Mother of All: for you wander in heaven and seek out the wide, immeasurable abyss. <margin>2835</margin> You are the beginning and the end; you alone rule over all; for from you is everything, and in you, Eternal One, everything ends. 

You wear an eternal diadem around your temples, <margin>2840</margin> the unbreakable, unsolvable bonds of great Kronos <note>Saturn/Time</note>, and you hold a golden scepter in your hands. Kronos himself engraved the inscription all around <margin>2845</margin> your scepter; he gave it to you to carry, so that everything might exist eternally: 'Subduer, tamer of courage, tamer of men, tamer of necessity.' You rule over Chaos. <margin>ZW</margin> <note>original: "ZW" refers to a "Zauberwort" or magic word, indicating a secret name or formula should be inserted here</note>. 

Greetings, Goddess, and listen to your surnames. I sacrifice <margin>2850</margin> this spice to you, child of Zeus, arrow-shooter, heavenly one, protector of harbors, mountain-roamer, dweller upon the roads, goddess of the underworld and of the night. <margin>2855</margin>

### IV 2856—2914

...and underworld-dwelling, dark one; quiet and dreadful one <note>original: "daspliti," a Homeric epithet often used for the Furies or Hekate</note>, who has your feast among the graves, Night, 2860 Erebos, wide Chaos; for you are inescapable Necessity <note>original: "Ananke"</note>, you were Fate <note>original: "Moira"</note>, and you are a Fury <note>original: "Erinys"</note>, the touchstone, you the destroyer, you are Justice <note>original: "Dike"</note>. **Incense for the ritual:** For beneficial deeds, burn storax, myrrh, 2875 sage, frankincense, and fruit pits; but for harmful deeds, use the substance <note>original: "ousian," usually referring to hair or biological remains</note> of a dog and a spotted goat, likewise also of a maiden 2880 who died untimely. **Protection for the ritual:** Take a magnetite stone <note>original: "sideriten," literally "iron-stone"</note>, in which let a triple-faced Hekate be engraved; let the middle face be that of a horned maiden, the left that of a dog, and the one on 2885 the right that of a goat. <margin>Leaf 32r.</margin> **Attraction Spell.** Addressed to the star of Aphrodite <note>the planet Venus</note>. **Incense:** Blood and fat of a white pigeon, raw myrrh, and roasted wormwood; make these into pills together and 2895 burn them toward the star upon vine-wood or charcoal. ### IV 2915—2959

<margin>2915</margin> *thermidochê bareô[nê]*; **Compelling spell:** "Foam-born Cythereia <note>A title for Aphrodite, referring to her birth from the sea foam near the island of Cythera</note>, mother of gods and men, heavenly one, earthly one, Nature, mother of all, unsubdued, you who hold all things together, <margin>2920</margin> whirler of the great fire, you who possess the ever-moving, whirling, unbreakable Barzan <note>original: "Barzan," a magical name often identified with the Sun or the cosmic axis</note>; you fulfill all things, both head and feet. Sacred water is mixed by your wishes, whenever you move Rouzo <note>original: "Rouzo," an astral or angelic power associated with the stars</note> among the stars, the navel of the world which you possess. <margin>2925</margin> you drive pure desire into the souls of men, and women toward men; you make a woman lovely to a man for all days. Our Queen, Goddess, come to these incantations, Lady Arrhoriphrasi, Goetini, Cyprogeneia <note>original: "Kyprogeneia," meaning Cyprus-born, another title for Aphrodite</note>, *soui ês thnobochou*; <margin>2930</margin> *thorithê ethenepiô*, mistress *serthenebêêi*. And for [Name, daughter of Mother's Name], cast the torch of love so that she melts for me, [Name, son of Mother's Name], in affection for all days. And you, blessed Rouzo, grant this to me, [Name], as you rushed into your dance among the stars <margin>2935</margin> to be joined in the marriage bed against your will, and being led suddenly, you turned the great Barzan; and having been turned, you did not rest, but are shaken as you whirl... Lead [Name, daughter of Mother's Name] to me in affection and to my bed; and you, Goddess Cyprogeneia, <margin>2940</margin> fulfill this perfect incantation." If you see the star shimmering, it is a sign that she has been struck; if it is sparking, she is on her way; if it is elongated like a torch, she has already arrived.

<margin>Bl. 32v.</margin> **Attraction spell for sleeplessness.** Take the eyes of a bat while it is alive, then release it. <margin>2945</margin> Taking raw dough or unrefined wax, mold a small dog and place the right eye of the bat into the right eye of the dog, and the left likewise into the left. And taking a needle, thread the *ousia* <term>ousia: "substance," a technical term for personal items like hair or threads from a garment used to create a magical link to the target</term> <margin>2950</margin> into the needle itself, threading it through the eyes of the dog so that the *ousia* is visible. Put it into a new jar and seal it with a papyrus strip using your own ring which depicts crocodiles with their heads facing one another, and <margin>2955</margin> deposit it at a crossroads <note>original: "triodos," a place where three ways meet, sacred to Hekate</note>, marking the spot so that you can find it if you wish to retrieve it. The formula to be written on the papyrus strip: "I adjure you three times by Hekate *Phorphorba Baibô Phôrborba*, so that [Name, daughter of Mother's Name] may cast away the fiery [desire] in her eye..."

# IV 2915–2959

"...I adjure you, Cythera <note>An epithet for Aphrodite, the goddess of love, named after the island of Cythera</note> (magical words, including 'Aktiôphi, Ereshkigal,' the Word <note>original: "Logos," refers here to a specific magical formula</note>)." <margin>2915</margin> **Compelling prayer:**

> "Foam-born Cythereia, mother of gods and men, airy one, earthly one, all-mother Nature, unsubdued, you who hold all things together, <margin>2920</margin> who whirl the great fire in a circle, who hold the ever-moving, circling Barza <note>original: "Barza," a magical name for the cosmic axis or the celestial sphere</note> indissolubly; you create all things, head and feet, and according to your decrees the sacred water is mixed everywhere, whenever you move with your hands the <margin>2925</margin> Rouzo <note>original: "Rouzô," a name for a celestial entity or astral power</note> located beneath the stars, the center of the universe which you rule. You also guide sacred longing into the souls of men and women toward the man; and it makes the woman desired by the man every day. You, our Queen, Goddess, come to these incantations, <margin>2930</margin> august (magical words), born on Cyprus (magical words), Ruler (magical words), and cast love like a firebrand into her, [Name], daughter of [Name], so that she melts in longing for me, [Name], son of [Name], all her days. But you, Blessed <margin>2935</margin> Rouzo, grant this to me, [Name], just as you also compelled him, who did not want to join your choir of stars, onto the bed to unite with you; and being brought forward, he immediately turned the great Barza, and having been turned, he has not ceased and still moves in a whirl. Therefore, lead her, [Name], daughter of [Name], to me for love and the bed. But you, Goddess born on Cyprus, complete this incantation to its fulfillment." <margin>2940</margin>

If you see the star flash: it is a sign that she has been struck; if sparks fly: that she is on her way; but if it stretches out in length like a torch, she has already arrived.

### Sleeplessness-Inducing Sending Spell.

<margin>2945</margin> Take the eyes of a bat and release it alive again; and take raw dough made of wheat flour or unbaked wax, form a little dog and insert the right eye of the bat into the right eye of the dog, and likewise its left into its <margin>2950</margin> left. And take a needle, put the magical material <note>original: "Zauberstoff" (Greek: ousia), referring to personal items like hair or threads from the target used to create a sympathetic link</note> into this needle and push it through the eyes of the dog so that the magical material remains visible. Throw it into a new drinking vessel, provide it with a lead tablet, and <margin>2955</margin> seal it with a signet ring belonging to you, on which (two) crocodiles have their heads turned toward each other, and hide it at a crossroads after you have marked the spot so you can find it when you want to take it away. Prayer that is written on the tablet:
> "I adjure you three times by Hekate (magical words), that [Name] may lose the fire in her eye, or also... <margin>2960</margin>"

# IV 2960—3003

<margin>2960</margin> ...or also that she may lie awake, having no one in her mind except me, [Name], alone. I adjure you by the Maiden <note>original: "Korē," a title for Persephone</note> of the Crossroads <note>original: "Trioditis," an epithet for Hecate as goddess of the three-ways</note>, who is the true mother of [unclear] <margin>2965</margin> (whom you wish) [magical words] Brimo <note>original: "Brimô," a title for a terrifying chthonic goddess</note> [magical words]; all-seeing one, [magical word]; make [Name] lie awake for me through all [eternity].

Among the Egyptians, herbs are always gathered in this way: the root-cutter <term>rhizotomos: a specialist in gathering medicinal and magical plants</term> first purifies <margin>2970</margin> his own body, first sprinkling himself with natron <note>a naturally occurring mineral salt used for ritual cleansing</note> and censing the herb with resin from a pine tree, after carrying it three times around the place. Then, after censing it with kyphi <note>original: "kuphi," a complex Egyptian incense mixture</note> and pouring a libation of milk with prayers, he pulls up the plant while calling by name <margin>2975</margin> upon the divine spirit <note>original: "daimon"</note> to whom the herb is dedicated, for whatever use it is being taken, and appealing for it to become more effective for that purpose. The invocation he speaks for every herb, generally during the act of picking, is as follows:

> "You were sown by <margin>2980</margin> Cronus, you were conceived by Hera, you were preserved by Ammon <note>An Egyptian creator god often identified with Zeus</note>, you were born of Isis, you were nourished by Rainy Zeus <note>original: "ombriou Dios"</note>, you were grown by the Sun and the dew. You are the dew of all the gods, you are the heart of <margin>2985</margin> Hermes, you are the seed of the ancestral gods, you are the eye of the Sun, you are the light of the Moon, you are the zeal of Osiris, you are the beauty and the glory of the Heaven, you are the soul of the divine spirit of Osiris which revels in every place, you are the breath <margin>2990</margin> of Ammon. Just as you have exalted Osiris, so exalt yourself and rise, just as the Sun rises every day. Your height is equal to the Sun at its mid-heaven <note>The highest point in the sky</note>, and your roots are from the <margin>2995</margin> depths, but your powers are in the heart of Hermes; your stalks are the bones of Mnevis <note>The sacred bull of Heliopolis, associated with the Sun god Ra</note>, and your flowers are the eye of Horus, your seed is the seed of Pan. I wash you with resin just as I wash the gods; I do this for my own health. Be purified by my prayer and give us power like Ares and Athena. <margin>3000</margin> I am Hermes! I take you with Good Fortune <note>original: "Agathē Tyche"</note> and the Good Spirit <note>original: "Agathos Daimon"</note> and at a favorable hour and on a favorable day that is successful for all things."

After saying these things, he wraps the harvested herb in a clean linen cloth (and into the place of the root...)

⟨Lifting of Plants.⟩ Among the Egyptians, (magical) plants are always lifted in this way: The root-cutter <term>rhizotomos: a specialist in gathering medicinal and magical plants</term> first performs a purification of his own person. First, he sprinkles himself all around with natron <note>a naturally occurring mineral salt used for ritual cleansing</note> and censes the plant with <margin>2970</margin> pine resin, carrying it three times around the spot. Then he burns kyphi <note>a complex, sacred Egyptian incense mixture</note>, pours a libation of milk, and pulls up the plant while reciting prayers, naming the divine spirit <note>original: "daimon"</note> to whom the plant is dedicated, and the purpose for its <margin>2975</margin> lifting, while praying that it may become as effective as possible for that purpose. The invocation, however, which he speaks over every plant in general during the lifting, is this:

"You were sown by Cronus, conceived by Hera, protected <margin>2980</margin> by Ammon <note>an Egyptian creator god often identified with Zeus</note>, born of Isis, nourished by raining Zeus, and raised by Helios and the dew. You are the dew of all the gods, you are the heart of Hermes, you are the seed of the ancestral gods, you are the eye of Helios, you are the light of the Moon, you are the dignity of Osiris, you are the <margin>2985</margin> beauty and the radiance of Heaven, you are the soul of Osiris’s spirit <note>original: "daimon"</note> which wanders in every place, you are the breath of Ammon. Just as you have exalted Osiris, so exalt yourself and rise up, even as Helios rises every day. Your height is equal to the noon-height of Helios, <margin>2990</margin> but your roots (are equal to the roots) of the Abyss; your powers are in the heart of Hermes, your wood is the bones of Mnevis <note>the sacred bull of Heliopolis, associated with the sun god</note>, and your flowers are the eye of Horus, your seed is the seed of Pan. I <margin>2995</margin> wash you with resin just as the gods are washed, for the sake of my own health; be purified by prayer and give us strength like Ares and Athena. I am Hermes. I grasp you with Good Fortune and with a Good Spirit <note>original: "Agathos Daimon"</note> and <margin>3000</margin> at a good hour and on a good day, which makes all things succeed." When he (the root-seeker) has spoken this, he wraps the harvested herb in clean linen (but into the place of the root, the root-seekers sometimes threw seven grains of wheat and <margin>3004</margin> [barley]...)

### Critical Apparatus Notes
<note>
**3101** *synchythē ars.*: The scholar Hopfner suggests "the male-female All"; but see line 3124. 
**3102/03**: The tone is strongly rhythmic. 
**3103**: "and of the [realms]" (*kai tōn*): Likely dependent on "under" (cf. 3059). Eitrem suggests *katecheis* ("you hold") instead of *kratos echeis* ("you have power"). *paidalis* in the papyrus; Dieterich reads *paidolis*. 
**3104**: *stygardēs*: Perhaps a reference to Styx or Hades. *sankleon*: Perhaps related to the "Zanklon" or sickle. 
**3105**: *choirapsa*: Eitrem suggests "pig-squeezer." 
**3107**: "concerning a certain matter" (*deinos pragmatos*). *apostatheis*: "one who withdrew," possibly a mythological reference to Zeus being hidden from Kronos. 
**3114**: The papyrus repeats "concerning which you ask" from the previous line.
</note>

### House-Protecting Spell

### Dream-Vision of the Three Reeds

The "Dream-Burier" <note>original: "Oneirothauptane." Scholars suggest this is a scribal error for "Oneir-autoptane," meaning "Dream Self-Viewer" or direct dream vision</note> of the three reeds. The picking of the reeds takes place before <margin>3175</margin> sunrise. After sunset, pull up the first reed while looking toward the East and say three times: ‘Maskelli Maskello Phnoukentabaoth Oreobazagra <note>This "Maskelli" formula is a famous sequence of power-words used to invoke chthonic or underworld deities</note>, Earth-breaker, Horse-of-the-Earth, Fire-source-spinner; A E E I O O U <note>the seven Greek vowels representing the planets</note> Lepetai Azarachtharo, I pick you so that you may bring me a dream-vision.’ And <margin>3180</margin> pulling up the second while facing the South, say again the ‘Maskelli’ formula and the vowels and ‘Throbeia,’ and while holding the reed, turn around. Looking toward the North and <margin>Bl. 35r.</margin> the West <term>original: "liba," the southwest wind/direction</term>, say the same names three times—those used for the second reed. And pulling up the third, say the same names and these: ‘Ie Ie, I pick you for this specific deed.’ These are the names to be written on the reeds: on the first, <margin>3190</margin> ‘Azarachtharo’; on the second, ‘Throbeia’; on the third, ‘Ie Ie.’ 

Then take a lamp that has not been colored with red-earth, fill it with pure oil, and taking a clean rag, write out all the names. Speak the same words to the lamp seven times. <margin>3195</margin> Let the lamp face the East, and let a censer be placed nearby in which you will offer uncut frankincense. Having prepared the reeds and tied them together with palm fibers, [shaping] them into the form of a tripod, place the lamp upon them. Let the head of the practitioner <margin>3200</margin> be crowned with olive branches. 

Preparation of the ink with which you must write on the reeds and the wick: single-stalked mugwort, "compulsion-plant" <term>original: "katananke," a plant used in love and binding spells</term>, three stones <note>or "bones"</note> of Nicolaus dates <note>a high-quality variety of date named after Nicolaus of Damascus</note>, three Carian dried figs, gold-worker’s soot, three sprigs of a male date palm, <margin>3205</margin> and sea foam. These are the things to be written and invoked: ‘I adjure you, the one under [the power of] excellence <note>original: "arete"</note>, that I wish for you to enter into me and show me concerning [such-and-such] a matter: Ierorie-thedien-throu; Chaora; Arpebo; Endalela.’

### Dream-Vision without a Medium using Three Reeds

A ritual for a direct dream vision seen without the need for a child-medium, utilizing three reeds. The gathering of the reeds takes place before sunrise. After <margin>3175</margin> sunset, pull out the first reed and say, looking toward the East, three times: ‘(Magical Words, the 7 vowels, Magical Words), I pick you so that you may send me a vision in a dream.’ And <margin>3180</margin> when you pull out the second one, say again toward the South the Maskelli formula <note>A famous, long string of power-words used to invoke powerful cosmic and underworld forces</note> and the vowels and (Magical Words); while holding the reed, turn around; looking toward the North and toward the West, recite three times the same names <margin>3185</margin> as those of the second reed. And when you pull out the third one, say the same names and in addition: ‘(Vowels) I pick you for such-and-such a purpose.’ 

The following is written upon the reeds. On the first: (Magical Words); on the second: <margin>3190</margin> (Magical Words); on the third: (Vowels). Then take a lamp that is not colored red <note>meaning a plain, unglazed clay lamp</note>, fill it with pure oil, take a clean piece of cloth, and write all the names upon it. Recite the same names seven times toward the light. The light should face <margin>3195</margin> the East; a censer should stand next to it, upon which you must offer uncut incense. When you have bound the reeds together with date palm fiber—once you have brought them into the form of a tripod—then set the light upon them. The head of the magician <margin>3200</margin> should be wreathed with olive branches. 

The ingredients for the ink with which one must write upon the reeds and the wick: single-stemmed mugwort, compulsion-herb <term>original: "katananke," a plant believed to have the power to compel spirits or lovers</term>, pits of 3 Nicolaian dates <note>a high-quality variety of date named after Nicolaus of Damascus</note>, 3 Carian figs, soot from a goldsmith’s shop, 3 sprouts from a male date palm, and sea foam. The written <margin>3205</margin> and recited words are as follows: ‘I adjure you who are hidden in the magical power [of the plant]; because I wish for you to enter into me and reveal to me concerning the matter at hand (Magical Words).’

<margin>3210</margin> **Aphrodite’s Bowl-Divination** <note>original: "phialomanteia," a method of divination using a bowl of liquid</note>. After purifying yourself for 7 days, take a white bowl and fill it with water and oil. First, write on the bottom of the bowl using myrrh-ink <term>ink made by mixing myrrh with burnt soot or lamp-black</term>: ‘hioch chipha; elampser zel aeiouo’ (25 letters), and underneath the bottom <margin>3215</margin> on the outside: ‘Tachiel, chthonic <term>an underworld deity</term> one, draxo’ (18 letters), and seal it with white wax. Let the bowl be placed on the ground, and while gazing intently, say: ‘I invoke <margin>3220</margin> you, the mother and mistress of nymphs, Ilauch obrie louch tlor, enter <insert>into the light</insert>, holy light, and give an answer by showing your beautiful form.’ Then gaze into the bowl. When you see her, greet her and say: ‘Hail, goddess of great glory, Ilaraouch; if you are to oracle for me, stretch out <margin>3225</margin> your hand.’ When she stretches it out, make your request regarding the questions you have. But if she does not listen, say: ‘I invoke the Sun-Holder <note>original: "heliouchou"</note>, who gave birth to Himeros <term>the personification of Longing or Desire</term>, and you, the good Hours <note>the Horai, goddesses of the seasons and natural order</note> and <margin>3230</margin> the Graces <note>the Charites, goddesses of charm and beauty</note>. I invoke also the divine Nature of all things, two-formed, undivided, straight-pathed, foam-born Aphrodite <note>original: "aphroraian," referencing the myth of her birth from sea foam</note>, to show me your beautiful light and your beautiful face, O Lady Ilauch. <margin>3235</margin> I adjure you, Fire-Giver <note>original: "puridora"</note>, elginal, and by the great names: obrie tych; kerdynouchi-lepsin niou naunin iouthou thrige; tatiouth gertiath; gergeris; gergeri-e theithi.’ You should also make the request by the names of the <margin>3240</margin> all-wondrous ones: ‘oisia ei ei ao eu aao ioiaiaio eothou berbroi; Ray-Thrower <note>original: "akterobore"</note>, geri-e ieoua; bring me light and your beautiful face and a true bowl-divination <margin>3245</margin>, shining with fire, carried in fire, shaker of the earth, io io phthaie thouthoi phaephi. Perform!’

Use lamp-oil and pure river water. Place the cup on your knees and recite the inscription provided above, and the goddess will appear to you and give an oracle concerning whatever you wish.

## Aphrodite’s Bowl-Divination.

Keep yourself pure for 7 days; then take a <margin>3210</margin> white bowl and fill it with water and oil, after you have first written on its bottom with myrrh-ink <term>a ritual ink made from myrrh and vegetable soot</term>: (Magic words: 7 vowels, 25 letters). On the outside, under the bottom, write: ‘Tachiel, Chthonic One <note>original: "Unterirdische," referring to a deity of the underworld</note> (Magic words: 18 letters),’ and seal <margin>3215</margin> it there with white wax. On the upper rim, from the outside, write: ‘(Magic words, and below them ‘Aphriel’) I ask.’ Speak this three times. The bowl, however, should stand on the floor <note>original: "Estrich," referring to a paved or plastered floor</note>. And you, gazing intently, say: ‘I invoke you, the mother and mistress of the nymphs (Magic words), <insert>come</insert> in, holy light, and give an answer, <margin>3220</margin> showing your beautiful form.’ Then look sharply into the bowl. As soon as you see the goddess, greet her and say: ‘Greetings, Goddess, highly praised (Magic words); if you are willing to prophesy for me, stretch out your hand.’ If she stretches it out, <margin>3225</margin> then demand an answer to your questions. But if she does not listen, say: ‘I invoke the (Magic words) who created longing, who hears you, and you, good <margin>3230</margin> Graces <note>original: "Chariten," the goddesses of charm, beauty, and nature</note>, I invoke also the Nature of the Universe, sprung from Zeus, the double-formed, indivisible, day-loving <note>The translator notes a degree of uncertainty regarding "den Tag liebende?"</note>, swift, foam-beautiful Aphrodite, to show me your beautiful light and your beautiful face, O Mistress (Magic words). <margin>3235</margin> I adjure you, Fire-giver (Magic words), and by the great names (Magic words).’ Also make your demand by the all-beloved names: (Magic words, vowels, ‘Eater of the unburied’ <note>a dark, chthonic epithet for the goddess</note>). <margin>3240</margin> ‘Bring me light and your beautiful face and the true bowl-oracle, Fire-gleaming one, surrounded by fire, stirring up the land far and wide (Vowels, <margin>3245</margin> Magic words). Accomplish it.’

**Procedure:** When you have kept yourself pure, as you have learned, take a bronze drinking vessel and write the inscription provided above, which is called 'Aphrodite's,' using myrrh-ink. For the filling, use <margin>3250</margin> lamp oil and pure river water. Place the cup on your knees and recite the column of text written above over it, and the goddess will appear to you and reveal whatever you desire.

Take a raw brick and, using a bronze stylus, carve onto it a <margin>3255</margin> running donkey. On its forehead, write: (Vowels); on its neck in the shape of a bell: (Vowels); on its back: (Magic words); and on its chest: ‘Sabaoth’; under its feet: ‘Abrasax’ <note>Sabaoth and Abrasax are powerful names of God frequently used in Greco-Egyptian magic</note>. Smear it with the blood of Typhon <note>likely referring to a red substance or a specific plant associated with the god Seth-Typhon</note> and a pig, and with onion juice. <margin>3260</margin> The prayer which is written on the brick is as follows: (Typhonian names, Magic words), who shakes (Magic words), who shakes the universe: I invoke you <margin>3265</margin>

->**P V.**<-

Greek Papyrus 46 of the British Museum. A collective manuscript containing 10 magical instructions, a book of 489 lines on 7 leaves. The first leaf is evidently missing. The layers are no longer connected to each other, broken in the middle like P IV. Size: 28 x 21 cm, Recto and Verso written continuously in uncial script of the 4th century AD. Illustrations are inserted on Leaf 2r (an Eye of Horus between the 7 vowels), Leaf 5v (a Z-ring with magical characters, words, and a petition); the image promised in lines 171ff. was not drawn in.

First mention of P V: List of Additions British Museum 1836—40, London 1843, acquired 1839, p. 21: ‘Greek Pap. consisting of 7 leaves, written on both sides . . . and containing on an average thirty-seven lines in a page. It appears to be a fragment of a gnostic work, and commences . . . <note>original: "ον λογον εξορκιζωσε κατα των αγιων ονοματων" — "the word I adjure you by the holy names"</note>’, with which the beginning of Leaf 2, line 76 begins—

...is meant. On the inside of the box lid is written: ‘30 Oct. 1839 No. 4 Greek in 7 well-preserved leaves,’ and on the outside: ‘1839 Purchased from Anastasi No. 4.’ Legge, in the *Proceedings of the Biblical Archaeology Society* 23, 42, provides the note for P V and VI: ‘purchased in Thebes.’

First edition by Ch. W. Goodwin, *Fragment of a Graeco-Egyptian Work upon magic*, Publications of the Cambridge Antiquarian Society II, Cambridge 1852, with 1 facsimile. This lithograph reproduces the image of the *Krikos* <note>a magical ring or circle</note>. Includes text, English translation, and factual commentary. The next edition was by Wessely, 1888, who had already shared the *Logos* <note>the sacred or magical word</note> of the Z-ring in 1886. A new treatment by Kenyon, *Greek Papyri* 1, 1893, pages 64–81, with photographic plates 36–49. (See also Kenyon, *Palaeography of Greek Papyri*, 1899, p. 115, regarding the book format.) Supplements to Wessely and Kenyon were provided by Ulrich Wilcken (1894), and textual criticisms by W. Kroll (1894/1895). Certain parts relating to revelation magic were treated and translated by Theodor Hopfner in *Revelation Magic II*. Further literature is listed below in the appropriate places and in the overview by Preisendanz. P V has been newly collated by me.

<meta>This page continues the rituals from the London-Leiden Papyrus (PGM V). The previous page established the scholarly provenance of the manuscript, which was purchased in Thebes in 1839. We are currently in the middle of a ritual involving a "boy medium" and a vision of a divine throne.</meta>

### Ritual of Marianos
18 **Of Marianos:** (akrabaeo ephiazēle arbamenothi ēō namisphrēti) <note>These are *voces magicae*, or "magical words," believed to have power through their sound rather than their literal meaning.</note>, appear and strike awe into 20 the one who appeared before fire and snow, **Bainchoooch** <note>original: "Βαϊγχωωωχ"; a powerful solar name in Egyptian magic, often associated with the soul of the sun</note>. For you are the one who revealed light and snow, you with the terrifying face, thunderer and lightener, swift-footed one; pintouche etōm. **Thoth**; thasinaēak arourongoa **Patha**; enōsade; **Iaē**; **Iaō ai**; aoiaō; eoēu (a nine-letter name).

Perform the first letter with the mouth open, like a wave; the 'o' with a rounded mouth as a spiritual threat; the 'iaō' for earth, air, and heaven; the 'e' like a dog-headed baboon <note>original: "κυνοκεφαλιστί"; referring to the cry of the cynocephalus, the sacred baboon of Thoth</note>; the 'o' likewise, as mentioned before; 30 the 'ē' with pleasure, breathing deeply; the 'u' like a shepherd, drawn out long. If the spirit says, "I am giving an oracle," say: "Let the throne of the god enter: thronouza tera kyma; kyma; lyageu; apsitadrys; 35 gē molian-dron; bonbilion; peuchrē; let the throne be brought in." If it is carried in by four men, you ask: "Why are they wearing crowns, and what precedes the throne?"
<margin>Leaf 1 verso</margin>
40 If he says: "They are crowned with olive branches and a censer precedes it," then the boy is telling the truth.

---

### Dismissal
"Depart, Lord, to your own world and to your own thrones, to your own arches, and preserve me and this boy unharmed, in the name of the highest god, **Samas Phrēth**." Perform this when the moon is in a fixed zodiac sign, accompanied by beneficial planets, or in "good bounds" <note>An astrological term referring to specific degrees of a sign ruled by a lucky planet like Jupiter or Venus.</note>, while the moon is not full. 50 For this is better, and in this way the divination is performed in an orderly fashion. However, in other copies it was written: "when the moon is full."

---

### Ritual for Direct Vision
"eeim; to; eim; alalēp; barbariath; menebreio; Arbathiaōth; **Iouēl**; **Iaēl**, ounēēie; mekommias. Let the god who gives me the oracle come and 60 let him not depart until I dismiss him. our-naour; soul; zakoull; ougot; nooum-biaou; thabrat; beriaou; achthithi; maraï; elpheōn; tabaōth; kirasina; lampsourē; **Iaboe**; ablamathanalba; akrammachamarei." Use this in a bronze cup over oil. 65 Anoint the right eye with water from a shipwrecked boat and the left eye with Coptic stibium <note>A dark mineral powder used as eyeliner, here specifically the Egyptian variety from Coptos.</note> mixed with the same water. If you do not find water from a shipwrecked boat, use water from a sunken river-skiff.

---

<note>Notes on the text:</note>
<note>Lines 14 f. They were clumsily and misleadingly inserted between the lines and at the top of the page. Line 18: "ph" was deleted by a dot and stroke, with "ch" written above as a correction. Line 20: "astrapte" (thunderer) has a "t" over "pa". Line 21: Scholars suggest "thasin aēak" might be "anak" (meaning "I am"). Line 23: Vowels marked with lines in the original. Line 24: The text suggests the pronunciation should sound "like the roaring of waves." Line 25: "o" is used for "spiritual threat," perhaps a commanding tone toward the appearing deity. Line 27: "like a baboon" refers to the ritualistic barking sounds associated with Thoth. Line 30: "shepherd-like" suggests a whistling or calling sound. Lines 31-40: These test the validity of the vision by asking the medium to describe specific details of the divine procession.</note>

### Stele of Jeu the Painter regarding the Letter:
"I call upon you, the **Headless One** <note>original: "ἀκέφαλον"; also interpreted as the 'Bornless One,' a deity without a beginning</note>, who created earth and heaven, who created <margin>100</margin> night and day, you who created light and darkness. You are **Osoronnophris** <note>original: "‘Οcοροννωφριc"; from the Egyptian 'Wsir-Wn-nfr,' meaning 'Osiris the Good Being'</note>, whom no one has ever seen; you are <margin>105</margin> **Iabas**, you are **Iapōs**. You have distinguished the just and the unjust; you have made female and male; you have revealed seed and fruits; you have made men to love one another and to hate one another. <margin>110</margin> I am **Moses** your prophet, to whom you committed your mysteries which are celebrated by **Israel**; you have revealed the moist and the dry and all <margin>115</margin> nourishment. Hear me! I am the messenger of **Phapru Osoronnophris** <note>original: "Φαπρω ‘Οcοροννωφριc"; 'Phapru' likely means Pharaoh or King</note>. This <margin>Bl. 2ᵛ</margin> is your true name, which was handed down to the prophets of **Israel**: Hear me, **Arbathiaō reibet . atheleberēth . ara blatha , albeu · ebenphchi · chitasgoē · Ib Aōth Iaō**. Hear me and turn away <margin>120</margin> this demon!"

### <Diebszauber:> Spell to Catch a Thief:
Take raw garlic and oxtongue <note>original: "Ochsenzunge"; likely the herb bugloss (*Anchusa*)</note>, press them, and burn the leftover pulp. Mix the ash properly with the juice, and with this mixture, write a "great eye" upon a wall. "I call upon you, the **Headless One** <term>Akephalos: literally "the one without a head," a powerful deity often identified with Osiris or the sun-god</term>, who created the Earth and the Heaven, who created the Night and the Day, you, who created the Light and the Darkness; you are the Good Osiris <note>original: "Osiris Unnefer"</note>, whom no one has ever seen; you are Iabas, you are Iapôs; you have separated the Just and the Unjust; you have created Female and Male; you have revealed Seed and Fruits; you have made humans love one another and hate one another. I am the Angel of the Benefactor <note>original: "Wohltäters"; likely a translation of the Greek "Euergetes" or Egyptian "Unnefer"</note>. This is your true name, which was passed down to the prophets of Israel. Hear me: <note>original: "ZW"; magic words</note>, hear me and turn away this demon. I call upon you, who are in the empty void of the air, the mighty—"

<margin>185</margin> **Spoken rite of the bread and cheese:** "Come to me <note>original: 'lission materna mauertê preptektioun intikious olokotous'—these are likely corrupted Latin or Greek magical sounds</note>, so that you may surround me, bring back the lost item to me, and make the thief manifest on <margin>Bl. 3ʳ</margin> this very day. **The Procedure:** The same spoken rite is used during the purification. Taking a turquoise-colored vessel, put in water and myrrh and dog’s-head plant <term>cynocephalion: likely a plant such as the snapdragon, named for its shape</term>, and soaking a branch of laurel, <insert>sprinkle</insert> <margin>200</margin> <margin>[Bl. 4ᵛ]</margin> each person to purify them. Taking unsalted wheat bread <note>original: 'selignion'</note> and <margin>205</margin> goat cheese, give to each person eight drachmas of the bread and eight drachmas of the cheese, reciting the following spoken rite. Also, write this name and stick it beneath the tripod: "**Master Iao**, <margin>210</margin> **light-bringer, hand over the thief** whom I seek." If any of them fails to swallow what was given to him, he is the one who stole.

After first purifying yourself from all things, take the ring and place it into the oil; then offer the kyphi and myrrh upon the censer. Leave it for three days, and then <margin>230</margin> take it and put it away in a clean place. For the consecration, let there be laid out pure loaves of bread and whatever fruits are in season. After making another sacrifice upon wood of the <margin>Bl. 4ʳ</margin> <margin>235</margin> vine, during the sacrifice, take the ring out of the oil and put it on. Use the ointment from the vessel to anoint yourself every morning, and standing toward the rising of the sun, say the <margin>240</margin> words written below.

# V 247–310

"I am **Thoth**, the inventor and creator of medicines and letters; come to me, you who are under the earth, rouse <yourself> for me, the great spirit, **Phnoun**, the one of the underworld <note>original: 'Phnoun' or 'Nun', the Egyptian god of the primeval waters and the abyss</note> (or the Nuns, the ones of the underworld). I am the glorious **Heron** <note>Heron was an Egyptian deity often identified with the Agathodaimon or 'Good Spirit'</note>, the egg of the ibis, the egg of the falcon, the egg of the air-roaming **Phoenix**. Having under my tongue the mud of **Em** <note>Em is likely a secret magical name for a primordial substance or deity</note>, I am clothed in the skin of **Keph** <note>likely referring to the baboon-headed 'Cynocephalus,' an animal sacred to Thoth</note>. If I do not know what is in the souls of all people—Egyptians, Greeks, Syrians, Ethiopians, and every race and every nation—if I do not know what has happened and what is going to be, if I do not know their arts and their pursuits and their works and their lives and their names and the names of their fathers and mothers and brothers and friends and those who have died, I will pour out the blood of the black-eyed dog <note>A reference to Anubis, the jackal-headed god of embalming</note> into a new, unmoving pot and I will set it 
<margin>Folio 4, verso</margin> 
upon a new brazier, and I will burn the bones of the **Hesiēs** <note>The 'Hesiēs' refers to the 'Drowned One,' specifically Osiris, who was drowned in the Nile. To burn his bones was a supreme magical threat to cosmic order</note> and I will cry out in the harbor of **Busiris** <note>A city in the Nile Delta, the mythological burial place of Osiris</note> for the one who remained in the river for three days and three nights, the Hesiēs, the one who was carried in the flow of the river into the sea, who was encompassed by the waves of the sea and by the clouds of the air. Your belly is eaten by the fish, and I will not stop the fish from chewing your body with their mouths, nor will the fish ever close their mouths. I will take the **Fatherless One** <note>Horus, the son of Osiris, who was born after his father's death</note> away from his mother, the sky-pole will be cast down, and the two mountains will become one. I will let loose an opening upon you <note>likely referring to the serpent-demon Apophis or a cosmic breach</note>, and he shall do what he wishes. I will not allow a god or goddess to give an oracle until I, [Name], discern what is in the souls of all men—Egyptians, Syrians, Greeks, Ethiopians, every race and nation—those who question me and those who come into my sight, those who speak and those who are silent, so that I may announce to them what has happened to them in the past, their present circumstances, and what will happen to them in the future; and so that I may know their arts and their lives and their pursuits and their works and their names and the names of the dead and of all people, and so that I may read a sealed letter and report everything to them according to the truth."

<margin>Folio 5, recto</margin> 
**The Ritual Procedure:** Taking a sheet of priestly papyrus or a lead leaf and an iron ring, place the ring upon the papyrus and, both inside and outside the ring, trace the shape of the ring with a reed pen. Then, mark the circumference with myrrh-ink, then write upon the circumference of the

<note>Scholarly Commentary on the lines above:</note>
**246/47** Paragraph marker. **249** "Rouse <yourself>" — suggested correction by Preisendanz. **251** "Phnoun" — from the Coptic word for "Ocean," "Abyss," or the god of the primordial waters. "Heron" — Wessely suggests this is "Hero," while Reitzenstein connects it to the Good Spirit. **254** "Em" — Hopfner suggests "Em is your name" based on other papyri. **255** Hopfner explains "Keph" as shorthand for "Cynocephalus" (baboon), meaning the magician says "I have put on the skin of the baboon and become Thoth." **256–288** These lines are translated and discussed by scholars like Hopfner and Delatte regarding the "threats" used in magic. **267** "Black-eyed dog" — Refers to Anubis. **270–273** "Hesiēs" — Specifically the drowned Osiris; a common figure in magical threats to force the gods' compliance. **282** "Fatherless One" — Horus. **284** "The two mountains" — Refers to an Egyptian myth about mountain ranges that could close and destroy Egypt or block the Nile (Osiris). **285** "Opening" — Possibly referring to Apophis, the chaos serpent.

### V 310–369

...of the ring, writing upon the papyrus <note>original: 'chartes'</note> the name, and the characters <note>magical symbols or signs</note> on the outside, then on the inside what you wish not to happen, and: "Let his mind <note>original: 'phronesis'</note> be bound <margin>315</margin> so as not to do this specific thing." Then, having placed the ring upon its own circumference which you drew, and having taken up the parts outside the circumference, sew the ring until it is completely covered. While stitching through the characters <margin>320</margin> with the reed-pen and binding them, say: "I bind [Name] to such-and-such; let him not speak, let him not resist, let him not <margin>325</margin> speak against me, let him not be able to look me in the eye or speak back, but let him be subject to me as long as this ring remains buried. I bind his mind and his wits, his thoughts, his actions, so that he is sluggish toward all people." <margin>330</margin> If for a woman: "So that [Name] does not marry [Name]" (and the usual common phrases). Then, <margin>Bl. 5ʳ</margin> having carried it to the grave of one who died untimely <note>original: 'aoros' — those who died young or violently were believed to be restless and more easily reached by magicians</note>, dig down four fingers and deposit it and <margin>335</margin> say: "Ghostly spirit <note>original: 'nekydaimon'</note>, whoever [you] may be, I deliver [Name] to you, so that he does not do this specific thing." Then, after burying it, depart. It is better to do this during a <margin>340</margin> waning moon. These are the things written in the circle: "**aroa mathra; Ereschigal <note>The Sumerian Queen of the Underworld, often equated with Hecate in these papyri</note>; edanta; iabou ne; ake; Iao <note>The Greek transcription of the Hebrew name for God, Yahweh</note>; darynko; Maniel**; let this specific thing not be done for as long a time as this ring is buried." Bind it with bonds by making <margin>345</margin> cords and thus deposit it. The ring can also be thrown into an unconsulted <note>original: 'achrematiston' — a well that is not currently in use or is used for sacred purposes</note> well or near one who died untimely. After the characters, write also these things below the ring <margin>350</margin> in a rectangular block <note>original: 'plinthion'</note>: "**archool; Lailam; Semesilamph; ammophorion; ioae; phthouth; eo Phre <note>The Egyptian Sun God, Ra</note>**, the greatest spirit <note>original: 'daimon'</note>, **Iao, Sabaoth <note>Hebrew for 'Lord of Hosts'</note>, Arbathiao, Lailam, Osornophris <note>original: 'Osornophri' — a Greek form of the Egyptian 'Osiris-Wennefer,' the 'Beautiful Osiris'</note>, em Phre Phre, Phtha <note>The Egyptian creator god, Ptah</note> chroio Iao baboure thimam en Phre renousi Sabaoth Barbathiao thachra oucheeth Esornophri**", and the whole 59-letter name (above), which you also write on the inside. (See the image of the ring; <margin>Bl. 6ʳ Plate III 6</margin> the same procedure is written on a lead tablet, and after inserting the ring, wrap it in gypsum. After <margin>361</margin> the rectangular block below and the formula of **Iaeo**, also these: "**bakaxichuch menebaichuch Abraxas <note>A solar deity of high power, whose name's letters add up to 365 in Greek numerology</note> au**, restrain this specific thing." ### V 311–369

...the name, but the magical signs <note>original: 'charakteres' — specialized occult symbols</note> on the outside, and then on the inside, write what you wish not to happen, and this: "Let his reasoning be bound, <margin>315</margin> so that he cannot carry out such-and-such." ### V 370—420

<margin>370</margin> Take "heart-leaves" <note>original: 'enkardiou' — referring to the tender, innermost leaves</note> of laurel and "virgin earth" <note>earth from a place never before plowed or built upon</note> and seed of artemisia, <margin>372</margin> flour, and the herb called "dog-head" <note>original: 'kynokephalion' — likely snapdragon or a similar plant resembling a dog's head</note>. (I have also heard <margin>374</margin> from a man of Heracleopolis that he instead takes fresh shoots from a renowned olive tree). Let these be carried by a <margin>376</margin> pure boy <note>a child who has not yet reached puberty, considered ritually untainted</note>. Grind these materials together with the others and add the fluid of an ibis egg to the whole mixture. Shape it into a figure of Hermes <margin>379</margin> wearing a cloak <note>original: 'chlamydephoros'</note> while the moon is rising in Aries, Leo, <margin>380</margin> Virgo, or Sagittarius.

Let the Hermes figure hold a herald’s staff <note>original: 'kerykeion' — the caduceus</note>. Write the formula onto priestly papyrus <margin>382</margin> and into a goose bladder (as the man from Heracleopolis again suggests) and insert it <margin>384</margin> into the statuette for the purpose of "animation" <note>original: 'enpneumatoseos' — the ritual act of breathing life or spirit into a man-made object</note>. Whenever you wish to consult it, take papyrus and <margin>386</margin> write the formula and the specific request. Cut a hair from your own head and wrap it <margin>388</margin> in the papyrus, tying it with a reddish-purple <note>original: 'phoinikino'</note> knot. Place an olive branch outside it <margin>390</margin> and lay it at the feet of the Hermes (some say: place it upon the figure itself).

The statuette should be kept in a shrine made of linden wood. When you wish to consult the god, place the shrine <margin>393</margin> with the god inside near your head. Perform the invocation while offering frankincense upon an altar, along with <margin>395</margin> earth from a wheat-bearing field and a single lump of Ammoniac salt <note>original: 'halos ammoniakou' — a high-quality rock salt from the Oasis of Siwa, associated with the god Amun</note>. Let it lie near your <margin>397</margin> head, and go to sleep after saying the following, giving an answer to no one:

<margin>400</margin> "Hermes, ruler of the world, dweller in the heart, circle of the moon, round and square, <note>this refers to the dual nature of Hermes, both as a 'herm' (a square pillar) and his celestial, cyclical aspects</note> leader of the words of the tongue, <margin>403</margin> master of persuasion and justice, wearer of the cloak, wearer of winged sandals, <margin>405</margin> whirling through the ethereal path and beneath the depths of the earth, charioteer of the spirit, eye of the sun, greatest one, leader of the all-sounding tongue, <margin>409</margin> gladdening with your torches those beneath the depths of the earth—the mortals who have finished their lives. You are called the Foreknower of Fates <margin>412</margin> and the Divine Dream, who sends forth oracles by day and by night. Heal all the pains of mortals <margin>414</margin> with your cures. Come, blessed one, greatest son of Memory <note>original: 'Mneme' — Mnemosyne</note> who brings thoughts to completion. Appear in your own form <margin>417</margin> with a joyful countenance; appear to a holy man and send a joyful form to me, [name], so that I may <margin>420</margin> receive you through your virtues in prophetic arts. I beg you, Lord!"

### V 370—420

Take 28 leaves from a laurel tree that already has pith (but <margin>370</margin> I heard from a man from Herakleopolis that he takes 28 newly sprouted leaves from a cultivated olive tree, the well-known tree), virgin earth <note>earth that has never been plowed or used for construction</note>, <margin>375</margin> seeds of wormwood, wheat flour, and dog-head grass <note>original: 'kynokephallion'—an herb, possibly snapdragon, associated with the baboon-headed form of Thoth/Hermes</note>—these are to be gathered by an uncorrupted boy <note>a child who has not yet reached puberty, considered ritually pure</note>. Also, the fluid of an ibis egg is to be mixed with the aforementioned ingredients into a consistent dough to form a figure of a cloak-wearing Hermes <note>original: 'chlamydephoros'—referring to the 'chlamys', a short riding cloak worn by Greek messengers</note>, when the moon is rising in Aries, Leo, Virgo, or Sagittarius. The <margin>380</margin> Hermes should hold a herald’s staff <note>original: 'kerykeion'—the caduceus</note>; and write the prayer on hieratic papyrus <note>a high-quality grade of papyrus used by Egyptian priests</note> or on the windpipe <note>trachea</note> of a goose (as I heard again from the man from Herakleopolis), and insert this into the figure for its animation <note>the 'breathing of life' into the statue</note>. And if you <margin>385</margin> desire a prophecy, take a piece of papyrus and write the prayer and the question upon it, cut a hair from your own head, wrap it in the papyrus, tie it with a purple thread, wrap an olive branch around the outside, and place it at the feet of the Hermes (others say: place it upon him). The <margin>390</margin> figure, however, should stand in a shrine made of lime wood <note>linden wood</note>. When you desire a prophecy, place the shrine with the god at your head, recite the prayer, and burn frankincense upon an altar along with earth from a place that <margin>395</margin> bears grain, and a lump of salt of Ammon <note>original: 'ammoniakon'—sal ammoniac, often sourced from near the temple of Zeus-Ammon in Libya</note>. Let the Hermes stand at your head, and after the recitation, go to sleep without giving an answer <note>speaking</note> to anyone.

<note>original: "Zauberbild". In the context of these papyri, a "magical image" is a ritual drawing intended to be inscribed on the papyrus or a separate material (like lead or gemstone) to give the spell physical form and potency.</note>

***

<image-desc>A faint black and white reproduction of a drawing on a heavily textured surface, possibly papyrus. The image shows a central vertical structure, identified as a tripod—a three-legged stand often used in antiquity for religious offerings or by oracles. A winding shape is coiled around this stand, identified as a snake. The vertical grain of the papyrus material is very pronounced in this fragment.</image-desc>

**Figure 4: Snake around a tripod, Papyrus III, lines 196–197.**

<note>The tripod and the serpent are classic symbols of the Oracle at Delphi. In Graeco-Egyptian magic, these symbols often represent the god Apollo or the acquisition of prophetic knowledge.</note>

<term>Tripod (Dreifuß): A three-legged piece of furniture or altar, specifically the one used by the Pythia (priestess) at Delphi to deliver oracles.</term>

<term>Udjat (Utat): The Eye of Horus, an ancient Egyptian symbol of protection, royal power, and good health.</term>
<term>Krikos: Greek for "ring" or "circle." In magic, these circular diagrams often functioned as phylacteries (amulets for protection) meant to "bind" or contain power.</term>
<term>Charakteres: Non-linguistic "magical letters" or symbols often found in papyri and on amulets, believed to carry direct divine power.</term>
